articleTitle: Efficient Bi-Directional Charging Solutions for Compact Electric Vehicles for Sustainable Mobility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Green revolution and sustainability are the possible options in the present world scenario to reduce pollution levels and environmental hazards. Electric vehicles (EVs) are so far implemented as the leading alternative in the present market to meet sustainable goals. EVs have batteries that can store a lot of energy and assist the power grid through Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) initiatives during peak hours, called bi-directional technology. With increasing EV demand, the stress on the grid voltage profile also increases. Hence, implementing V2G and G2V technologies, which enable bidirectional energy flow, can solve this issue. In this work, small sizes of EVs are considered for the analysis. Considering the driving pattern of Guwahati city, India, the energy requirement for the particular EV is calculated. Also, regarding the growth rate of EVs, the future energy requirement in India is calculated. Additionally, a simulation technique is proposed for battery charging and discharging using a fuzzy logic controller (FLC), considering the per unit voltage of the grid and the state of charge (SOC) of the battery as input. The result shows that the battery will discharge towards the grid whenever the voltage profile is bad and the SOC is good.

articleTitle: Single OTRA Based Inverse Filter Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In this communication, a novel inverse filter configuration is introduced, demonstrating the capability to realize inverse filter responses, namely, inverse low pass filter (ILPF), inverse high pass filter (IHPF), inverse band pass filter (IBPF), and inverse band reject filter (IBRF), utilizing only one Operational Transresistance Amplifier (OTRA) along with a minimal number of passive elements. The proposed inverse filters are meticulously validated through simulations in Cadence PSpice, implemented in CMOS TSMC 0.18μ m technology. The simulated characteristics closely align with the theoretical results. Additionally, a comprehensive analysis encompassing non-ideal aspects, noise considerations, Monte Carlo simulations, and sensitivity analysis has been conducted.

articleTitle: Voltage Mode Sinusoidal Oscillator with Non-Interacting Adjustment of Parameters Employing VCII
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This article proposed a novel sinusoidal oscillator with quadrature voltage mode response employing a recently explored active element second-generation voltage conveyor (VCII). The derived oscillator configuration utilized three units of active device and four grounded/virtually grounded resistances along with two grounded capacitances. The adjustment between frequency of oscillation and condition of oscillation enjoys non-interactive controlling feature. Two distinct quadrature responses are available at the buffer ports of the device. The routine mathematical analysis includes the ideal analysis along with non-ideal, sensitivity, and parasitic parameters. The CMOS simulations of the proposed structure are carried out in a PSPICE environment with a TSMC 0.18µm parameter. Experimental verification for the same was performed by the commercially available chip AD844.

articleTitle: Digital Systems Influenced by Overflow Nonlinearities: A Robust Stability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This study presents criteria for evaluating the robustness of discrete-time systems (DTS) or digital systems that employ overflow arithmetic for their finite wordlength hardware and that are also subject to time-varying delays. The lower bound of the summation terms is obtained by employing a combination of Reciprocally Convex inequality (RCI) and Jensen's inequality; and Bessel Legendre inequality based on Legendre polynomials. This results in various criteria having the advantage of less computational burden for some criteria and less conservative results for others. Illustrative examples are provided for supporting the results.

articleTitle: A Novel Video Encryption Scheme Using Chaotic Map Based Simultaneous Permutation-Diffusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The need for robust video encryption is driven by the increasing demand for secure multimedia transmission and storage. Traditional encryption methods often fail to account for the high data volume and real-time constraints of video content. Chaos-based cryptography have intrinsic features like extreme sensitivity to initial conditions, deterministic, random, topological mixing, unpredictability. This paper presents a novel video encryption scheme using our earlier presented 2D Cosine-Sine chaotic map. The scheme comprises mainly five steps: (i) Retrieve each frame from the video separately and encrypts them one by one. (ii) The frame is converted into grayscale for simplicity. (iii) The Dynamic version of 2D Cosine-Sine map is created. (iv) The map is used to generate chaos matrix and chaotic sequence that is used for permutation and diffusion respectively. (v) We have introduced a simultaneous permutation and diffusion method in which as each pixel is permuted, it is immediately diffused before moving on to the next pixel. It reduces the need for multiple passes over the data, potentially speeding up the encryption process and enhance security. (vi)The grayscale frame is converted into BGR form. The efficiency of the scheme has been tested using various parameters.

articleTitle: Design of Efficient RAM Cell using Quantum-Dot Cellular Automata
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Quantum Dot Cellular Automata (QCA)-based Random Access Memory (RAM) cell design that enhances output voltage performance using a loop structure with a D-latch and specialized multiplexer configurations. It discusses QCA's advantages over CMOS technology in terms of area and power dissipation, making it promising for digital memory design. Additionally, the paper explores power usage, fault tolerance, and polarization effects in QCA technology to optimize RAM cell performance. The comparison with the state of art show that the proposed RAM is highly area efficient as the design requires lesser number of QCA cells. Moreover, the proposed RAM cell is highly time efficient, the clock latency is observed to be only 1.25 clock cycles.

articleTitle: Utilizing Transfer Learning for Automated Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) occurs when diabetes mellitus damages the blood vessels in the retina which is the part of the eye responsible for capturing images. This damage can cause vision problems or even lead to blindness if not addressed in time. Early detection and treatment are key to prevent serious vision loss from DR. However, diagnosing DR through manual examination of fundus images is both costly and time-consuming due to the need for trained medical professionals. Therefore, the development of automated DR detection systems is needed. This paper explores the use of transfer learning models, specifically VGG16, ResNet18, and AlexNet, on Fourier-Bessel series expansion (FBSE) based dyadic decomposition (FBD) decomposed images to detect DR. Transfer learning is crucial in medical image analysis since, it enables the development of accurate and efficient models even with limited data and computational resources. Network parameters are fine tuned and better features are extracted by applying the proposed approach. The results are computed over the benchmark dataset of DR. It is observed that our proposed approach based on ResNet18 network is giving the best performance and 92.15% accuracy is achieved.

articleTitle: Mean SNR Analysis of Different Diversity Combining Techniques Under Nakagami-m Fading Channels- A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This study provides an in-depth analysis of Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) performance for various diversity combining techniques under Nakagami-m fading scenarios. It primarily evaluates the SNR Gain of Equal Gain Combining (EGC) in practical fading situations. A generalized formula that can be applied to multiple fading environments—such as Rayleigh, Rician, and the worst-case conditions—is established. The Mean SNR Gains for different combining techniques are calculated, illustrated graphically, and compared across these fading conditions. The findings indicate that the Mean SNR Gain for Maximal Ratio Combining (MRC) is independent of the fading parameter, highlighting its effectiveness as the optimal combining technique.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow Using Dung Beetle Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper introduces a new dung beetle optimization (DBO) algorithm to solve optimal power flow (OPF) problem. The proposed method draws inspiration from the reproductive, ball-rolling, dancing, foraging, and thieving behaviors exhibited by dung beetles. By considering both local and global exploitation, the proposed method possesses the qualities of a rapid convergence rate and adequate solution precision. Along with equality and inequality constraints, the total generation cost, emission, active power loss, and magnitude of voltage deviation are considered as objective functions in this paper. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated utilizing the standard IEEE 30-bus test system. Furthermore, this research employs a penalty-based constraint handling approach to address various constraints associated with the OPF problem. The results obtained by the proposed method are contrasted with grey wolf optimization (GWO) algorithm. From results it is evident that the proposed method exhibits better performance with regard to convergence rate, solution accuracy, and stability.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of on Grid Solar Powered Electric Vehicles Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This research work aims to design and simulate an on-grid solar-powered electric vehicle (EV) charging station thereby addressing the issue of rising air pollution caused by vehicle exhaust emissions. Due to the depletion of fossil fuel supplies and the climate issue, electric vehicles (EVs) have appeared as the new face of this industry. Unless the electric vehicles are fuelled by renewable energy sources, the concept of them won't be truly sustainable. Multiple electric vehicles will be able to receive fast charging from the charging station at once. With a backup power supply from a battery bank for continuous charging even during power outages, the charging station will be built to work with the current power grid. Renewable energy will be produced by the solar panels that have been erected on the station's roof and utilised to power the electric cars. To analyse the charging station's performance in various traffic and weather circumstances, specialised software will be used in the simulation. The simulation results will aid in optimising the design of the charging station to ensure that it can charge electric vehicles quickly and effectively while having the least possible impact on the power system. The endeavour will help advance the use of renewable energy sources for transportation and support ongoing efforts to lower carbon emissions. Additionally, it will assist in addressing the rising need for infrastructure for electric vehicle charging, which is essential for the widespread use of electric automobiles.

articleTitle: Exponential Increase of Sustenance Time in the Air for a Quadcopter/Hexacopter Using an Extended Tethered Power Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The battery power with the use of Lithium Polymer (LiPO) Batteries is the only way presently to provide continuous power to a quad/ hexacopter. However, extending it to a respectable height for a longer duration is possible, if a power cable is used, in a similar manner, as the Kite is flown by a person from the ground. The power is extended with the help of the customized wire which is attached to the quadcopter/ hexacopter, which ultimately increases the overall endurance of the quad/ hexacopter from 20-30 minutes to 240 minutes (4 hours) in one run. The advantage achieved through such adjustments is that the quad/ hexacopter stays extended for that much time where a meaningful and successful study of the farflung area is made possible, which was earlier impossible to do.

articleTitle: Involutional Neural Network Based Approach for the Detection of Melanoma Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper presents an extraordinary method to detected melanoma, the most lethal form of skin cancer, using Involutional Neural Networks (INNs). Melanoma's early detection is crucial for effecacius treatment, yet existing diagnostic methods often lack the requiring precision and scalability. INNs offer a solve through their advanced capability to adaptively process spatial information in images, a huge different from traditional convolutional techniques. Our reaserch applies INNs to melanoma detectionair, focusing on their unique involution operations that significant enhance image analysis for accurately classification. The performance of our model, assessed across different metrics including accurate, precision, recall, and F1-scores, demonstrates its superior diagnostic capability. This investigation not only underscores the potency of INNs in medical imagining but also opens up new avenues for their application across diverse analytical needs in healthcare. By advancing melanoma detection methods, we contribute to the broader goal of improving early cancer diagnose and treatment outcomes!

articleTitle: Intelliseat Research Application Using Harmony Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Students safety and learning results are being impacted by this application in classrooms. The preferences for students or we can say unique needs for them are not being taken into account and traditional systems are may or may not be static. Such applications have changed the set up of how classrooms are being run. The technologies used in this system such as internet of things(IOT), Artificial Intelligence/Machine learning(AI/ML) & computer vision(OpenCV) to create a system which flexible, adaptable system which contribute in students life by enhancing their learning and keeping privacy of data which maintains their safety.

articleTitle: Improving the Growth of Jowar Millets in the Region of Uttar Pradesh Using Machine Learning and IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Agriculture is the main driver of the Indian economy, and technology is transforming conventional farming to increase productivity while reducing resource waste. Water scarcity is the biggest problem facing the globe today, mostly affecting the agricultural system. Consequently, a unique approach is taken while implementing the technology to increase agricultural output. This study aims to develop a smart irrigation system that utilises machine learning enabled by the Internet of Things (IoT) to automatically water plants and notify the user when needed. We have examined the jowar millets' development pattern in the Rampur region of Uttar Pradesh when there is a water shortage. Though it is grown south of Vindhyas, we have used our suggested model in this area because it requires little water. The gathered data is received by a cloud-based server, which saves it, interprets it, and applies machine learning to make irrigation recommendations. Field sensors are used in this project and the data they collect is stored on a cloud server. When deciding how much water to deliver, a decision-making tool called SVM is employed. SVM considers both soil moisture content and ambient temperature while determining how much water to disperse. With an accuracy rate of 99.8%, the SVM classifier is the best; it is closely followed by the RVM classifier, which has an accuracy rating of 98.8%. By contrasting each recommended strategy with earlier research, its efficacy is verified. Based on recognised performance indicators, the experimental results show that the recommended strategy performs better than comparable approaches.

articleTitle: Spectrogram Features and Xception Classifier Based Audio Spoof Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Voice biometric authentication has gained significant attention in recent years due to its non-intrusive and user-friendly nature. In this research paper, we present a comprehensive study on the effectiveness of three different spectrograms - Constant Q Transform (CQT), Mel and Gammatone at the front end of an Audio Spoof Detection (ASD) system. The back end of the system employs the Xception pretrained model. Our experimental results reveal that Gammatone Spectrograms outperform both CQT Spectrograms and Mel Spectrograms in terms of performance. Specifically, combination of Gammatone Spectrogram with Xception pretrained has achieved a remarkable 3.5% and 2% Equal Error Rate (EER) for ASVspoof 2021 DF and DECRO dataset, respectively

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Superior-Boost Quasi Z Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In this paper, various conventional topologies are discussed and compared with the proposed converter, namely the Superior Boost Quasi Z-source Inverter (SB-qZSI). The steady-state analysis of the proposed converter is conducted. Additionally, power loss and component design analysis is carried out, with the proposed concept providing half of the DC-link voltage across switch <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{7}$</tex>. This topology ensures continuous input current, shares a common ground, and experiences lower voltage and current stress while achieving high boost at low duty ratios. Furthermore, the proposed topology is compared with traditional Z-network topologies such as EB-qZSI, EBSC-qZSI, and UHG-qZSI. To validate the theoretical analysis, simulations are performed using MATLAB/Simulink employing simple-boost pulse-width modulation (PWM) technique. This topology configuration aims to overcome limitations by achieving a boost factor approximately equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2/(2(1-\overline{D})^{3}-1)$</tex>. where the duty ratio is constrained within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 < D < 0.206$</tex>. The proposed topology demonstrates satisfactory performance gains compared to traditional configurations.

articleTitle: Wavelet Based Bearing Fault Diagnosis Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Rotating parts of the machines are more vulnerable to faults, which leads to economic and life losses. In the proposed work, bearing fault detection is done using the wavelet and transfer learning approaches. In this work, four different motor conditions are considered healthy and bearing fault (ball, inner race, and outer race) under full load conditions. The manual feature extraction problem has been solved using the Continuous Wavelet Transform which converts the signal to an image, and features are extracted using the neural network model. Developing a convolutional neural network model from scratch is a tedious and lengthy process. This problem is solved using the AlexNet pretrained model for transfer learning. The pretrained models require tuning and optimisation as they are trained and tested over the different image classification problems. The tuning of the model is done in the fully connected layers, and optimisation is done by finding the best learning rate and the optimizer. The approach is reliable and accurate for bearing fault detection, as 100% accuracy has been achieved.

articleTitle: Variance Based Key-Frame Extraction Technique to Summarize Educational Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: As multimedia technologies advance, the education system is increasingly adopting e-Learning methods, such as e-classes, virtual classrooms, and online video lectures. This shift requires significant memory for storage and longer access times to manage multimedia content. Traditionally, students would take notes from blackboards or whiteboards at the pace of the lecturer. This work proposes key-frame extraction, a unique way of video summarizing, to give students with rapid access to relevant information. To assess the performance of the suggested model in comparison to cutting-edge models, both quantitative and qualitative experiments were carried out. Using two benchmark datasets, our key-frame extraction method demonstrated superior performance, achieving the highest F-measure.

articleTitle: Low Power CMOS Based Dual Edge Triggered Flip Flop Using LECTOR C-Element
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In the presence of signal interference and glitches, Double-Edge Triggered Flip-Flops (DETFFs) experience a substantial rise in power consumption. To address this issue and achieve power efficiency, this paper focuses on low-power DETFF utilizing LECTOR C-elements. The enhanced C-element integrated into DETFF effectively mitigates input signal glitches, inhibits unwanted transitions within the DETFF, and reduces the transistor's charge and discharge frequencies. LECTOR Circuit integrates two self-controlled leakage control transistors along the route from the power supply to the ground. This placement strategically introduces extra resistance, effectively diminishing the leakage current in the pathway. Further the optimized LECTOR C-Element reduces the delay by 15%. The utilization of these self-controlled transistors represents a promising advancement in mitigating leakage issues, showcasing potential improvements in the efficiency of CMOS circuits. In contrast to other currently available DETFFs, the DETFF introduced in this study undergoes a single flip exclusively at the clock edge and reduces the power consumption by 20%. The simulations were carried out by varying the Vdd voltage for the circuit form 0.6V to 1.2V on Cadence Virtuoso using GPDK-90 library and have the simulation results.

articleTitle: QCA Based Error Detection and Correction Circuit for Nano Communication Network Using Hamming Code
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Quantum-dot Cellular Automata (QCA) is an effective method used in nano communication coding circuits due to its extremely low energy consumption, great integration, and fast switching. The main objective of this paper is to design a Hamming Code circuit using QCA for Error detection and correction purposes. The Hamming Decoder at the receiver end has a Syndrome Calculator, 3:8 Decoder and an Error Corrector circuit. In this paper, a new reduced 3:8 decoder is designed with an optimization of 56% in cell count and 54% in area. A circuit for the (7,4) Hamming encoder is implemented based on the suggested structure with optimization of 50.5% by cell count and 75% by area. The overall Hamming code circuit architecture has been optimized by 15% in cell count and 8.11% by area. The QCADesigner has functionally validated the designs.

articleTitle: Comparison of Optimized Single-Pulse and Modified Single-Pulse Modes of Operation of Switched Reluctance Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The switched reluctance generator (SRG) is oper-ated in single-pulse mode (SPM) close to and above its base speed. SPM is characterized by two voltage pulses of equal magnitude and opposite polarity. Introducing a zero-voltage interval between the positive and negative pulses is known as a modified single-pulse mode (MSPM). This article proposes a comparative study of SRG performance operating with optimal methods of SPM and MSPM. Four optimal methods are considered in this work. Two optimal methods belong to SPM, and the other two optimal methods belong to MSPM. These methods optimize either rms phase current or rms dc-bus current for a given average dc-bus/output current of SRG. All four optimal methods are compared in terms of rms phase current, rms capacitor current, power loss, and efficiency of SRG drive. Both simulation and experimental results are provided. This work is helpful in choosing an appropriate operating mode between SPM and MSPM.

articleTitle: Single Sample Face and Ear Recognition using Transfer Learning and Sample Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Single-sample face and ear recognition is a challenging problem in biometrics due to the fact that only a single face or ear image sample is available for the training. However, during the recognition, test images may have possible variations like different poses, occlusion, brightness, etc, which increase the difficulty of the problem. Deep learning approaches have attracted researchers working in this area. However, the selection of proper methods for feature extraction and populating the training set for deep learning methods is still a challenge in this field. In this article, a method to solve the single-sample face and ear recognition problem is proposed that combines transfer learning with sample expansion to increase recognition accuracy. The proposed method uses sample expansion by intensity variation in random pixels before feeding the images to the VGG16 deep learning model with pre-trained ResNet50 weights on the ImageNet database for feature extraction. The proposed method is tested on two popular databases, ORL face and AMI ear databases. Accuracy results prove the effectiveness of the proposed method as it outperforms the conventional principal component analysis (PCA) feature extraction method by 26.51% and 46.47% in terms of classification accuracy on the ORL face and AMI ear database. This strengthens the assumption that deep learning models with appropriate sample expansion can be useful even in scenarios where we have smaller databases with limited or single training samples.

articleTitle: Smart Traffic Scheduling: A Real-Time Adaptive Approach for Unified Intersections
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Congestion at urban intersections significantly impacts traffic flow, air quality, and driver experience. Existing traf-fic control systems often rely on fixed timing plans, leading to sub-optimal performance. This paper proposes a novel framework for smart traffic control at unified intersections using Deep Q-learning. Our approach integrates real-time traffic flow analysis with adaptive signal timing adjustments, using dynamic input to the agent. The agent continuously learns an optimal policy for adjusting traffic signal phases and duration based on the observed traffic state, minimizing wait times and maximizing throughput. To address the non-stationary nature of traffic demand, we propose a real-time adaptive mechanism that continuously updates the model with new experiences. This ensures the system adapts to changing traffic patterns throughout the day. We evaluate our proposed framework through extensive simulations using realistic traffic datasets. Compared to traditional fixed-timing and reactive traffic control methods, our approach demonstrates significant improvements in average wait times, queue lengths, and overall intersection throughput. Furthermore, the real-time adaptability allows the system to maintain better performance even under unexpected traffic fluctuations.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Metal -to -Metal Contact RF-MEMS Switch for 6G Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This work presents two designs of wide-band ohmic switches tailored for 6G applications using RF MEMS technology. The switches are engineered to operate efficiently between 1GHz to 100GHz, with isolation surpassing -20dB(air gap=3μm) and insertion loss below -0.1dB. In both designs, the switching arm is integrated with the CPW line, with a 1μm to 3 μm gap in the transmission line,which representing the OFF state of the device. Actuation into the ON state is achieved via electrostatic force, collapsing the beam onto the transmission line. Analysis reveals that increasing the air gap enhances isolation in the off state. Additionally, the second design, featuring the switching arm in the broadside direction, exhibits higher insertion loss. Performance evaluations, including variations in metal types, offer valuable insights for optimizing both designs' insertion loss and isolation characteristics.

articleTitle: Wearables Based Personalised Stress Recognition using Signal Processing and Hybrid Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Wearable technology can assess physiological processes, which are known to be correlated with an individual's affective state. However, it is important to note that although there are generalised patterns, the nature of these associations might vary depending on the individuals involved. This study suggests using signal processing and deep neural networks as a means to tackle variations among individuals. Signal processing algorithms were developed for electrocardiogram (ECG), electromyography (EMG), and respiration signals. The stress recognition system was developed using a hybrid deep learning network consisting of long short-term memory and gated recurrent unit (LSTM-GRU) with attention layer. The LSTM-GRU with attention model was chosen due to its ability to handle time-series data and capture long-term dependencies, as well as its capacity to attend to the most informative features. Experiments were conducted on WESAD dataset physiological signals recorded from individuals during a stress-inducing task. The proposed method achieved an accuracy of 99.6% in stress recognition.The proposed method demonstrates the potential of using physiological signals as indicators of stress and highlights the importance of signal processing for accurate stress recognition. The results suggest that the LSTM-GRU with attention model is a promising approach for handling physiological signals in person-specific stress recognition tasks. This model has the potential to be useful in a variety of affective and medicinal applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Sentiment Analysis of Product Reviews
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: With the exponential growth of e-commerce, understanding consumer sentiments from online product reviews has become crucial for businesses. This study presents a comprehensive approach to online product review sentiment analysis, encompassing text and image data. To facilitate our research, we compiled a novel dataset from the Amazon e-commerce platform, comprising paired textual reviews, corresponding images and sentiment. The work employs a multimodal deep-learning approach to capture the nuanced sentiment expressed through both text and images. Specifically, we integrate the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model, enhanced with a low-rank adaptation to refine its self-attention mechanism, for textual sentiment analysis and the VGG16 neural network for image feature extraction. Our experiments demonstrate that this multimodal approach surpasses unimodal techniques, achieving convincing results in sentiment classification.

articleTitle: Investigation of VGG 16 Transfer Learning and CNN Integrated Brain Tumour Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This study had conducted an intensive exploration of the possibilities of VGG-16 and VGG-19 Convolutional Neural Network models for picture categorisation. Using a thorough method comprising substantial training and severe testing, we may observe both steady loss decrease and significant model accuracy improvements. It is assumed that the models may appropriately keep track of subtle variations in data to which they are adversarial while identifying regular patterns they may generalize. The VGG models’ architecture is quite sophisticated, but as seen above, they give strong classification accuracy, with performance in nearly ideal 99 percent in many trials. This integration proves that extremely advanced deep learning instruments are competent to handle and complete even very sophisticated picture recognition assignments. Additionally, our experiments identify a few essential aspects of model adjustment and tuning identifying important techniques considerably enhancing CNN outcomes in application scenarios. This study is pioneering for the automatic picture identification discipline since it provided a strong understanding of the generality and model quicker than many real-world models. Additionally, it exhibits that the CNN structures enhance artificial intelligence's power to recognize visual input and could improve many sectors like the surveillance and health systems. The findings defined here may now open the door to more progress in deep learning and picture process analyses while reiterated the importance of CNN in modern technology.

articleTitle: Impact of Various European and North American Standard Overcurrent Relays Characteristics on Optimum Coordination of DOCR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The coordination of overcurrent relays plays very important role as it plays very important role in protection of distribution system. Based on various standard and non-standard relays characteristic the optimum coordination can be achieved. Many researchers have proposed various nonstandard and standard relays characteristic to achieve the optimum setting of relay parameters. In this paper, two widely recognized standard models are utilized for overcurrent relays coordination. The first is known as the European Standard Model, which is based on the British Standard and IEC12 60255-151:2009 (BS142). The latter is the ANSI/IEEE C37.112-1996 standard-based North American, the standard model. In this paper, the impact of a few American based and a few European-founded overcurrent relays on coordination has been explored. Further, the previously reported objective function has been considered and after essential modification, optimum settings are achieved. A modified IEEE-14 bus test system is used to evaluate the performance of these relay's characteristic features is also investigated. For these two widely used standard models, the best overcurrent relay settings are obtained using a genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: VBRN2: Video Description using Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Comprehending recordings can greatly influence and benefit multiple applications. Yet, computer-generated de-scriptions frequently struggle to precisely reference objects in videos. This research seeks to resolve this challenge by integrating detailed visual information from all video frames. We provide a sequence-to-sequence model for creating video descriptions that is built on LSTM and improved with semantic attention. Our findings indicate that semantic attention, which selectively targets external fine-grained visual details, effectively helps the system reference objects in videos, leading to improved descriptions. Fur-thermore, we employ Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks to capture temporal relationships in the input frames in both forward and backward directions.

articleTitle: Modeling MoS2/Si Heterostructure for Broadband Photodetection in COMSOL Multiphysics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband photodetector based on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MoS}_{2}/\text{Si}$</tex> heterostructure. The device's optical per-formance was assessed by measuring responsivity, EQE, and photocurrent across a broad spectrum from 300 nm to 1100 nm. Illuminated with a constant low optical power of 1mW,the device's photocurrent was recorded. The device exhibits a maximum responsivity of 38.5 mA/W at NIR wavelength (960 nm) and 13 mAIW for the visible spectrum (750 nm). Compared to other <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MoS}_{2}$</tex> -based structures, the modeled device demonstrates improved performance. The modeling approach presented for this structure suggests a promising design strategy for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MoS}_{2}$</tex> - based optoelectronic devices at the nanoscale, with implications for the optoelectronics industry.

articleTitle: Beyond CMOS: Unlocking Low-Power with TFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper delves into the realm of energy-efficient electronics by exploring the prospects of Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors (TFETs) in facilitating low-power capabilities. By scrutinizing different TFET structures, including III-VTFETs, Heterojunction, Nanowire, Dual Material Gate, Gate-All-Around TFETs, and Double Gate TFETs, the study expounds on their unique design features. The analysis is a synthesis of previous research aimed at providing a comprehensive overview of TFET structures that can be valuable for academics and practitioners alike. This article extends beyond traditional CMOS and offers an insightful glimpse into the nascent field of energy-efficient electronics.

articleTitle: Electric Field Modulation in Gate-All-Around Nanosheet Transistor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The work consists of the study and mitigation of crowding of electric field around the edges and corners of Nchannel nanosheet transistor, as this crowding of electric field can result in localized high electric field strengths and reliability issues. The structural modification is done in the device's structure, which reduces the electric field crowding. The modified device also results in on current improvement. Also, the effect of gate and drain voltages on the electric field profile and the various electrical parameters are analyzed.

articleTitle: Stock Price Prediction using CABC Trained Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm is a prominent swarm-based optimization procedure. This meta-heuristic optimization procedure is structured over of the food-search behavior of natural honey bee swarms. CABC (Co-variance Guided Artificial Bee Colony), a powerful variant of ABC, is formed by combining ABC with the principles of statistical co-variance. In this article, CABC algorithm is used and tested for the optimization of neuron weights in an Artificial Neural Network. The tuned and trained Artificial Neural Network is then used to forecast the market movements of the three major stock market commodities, i.e. crude oil, gold, and silver. The performance of the suggested CABC based neural network training model is justified on the readings of Mean Error and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Obtained results exhibit that CABC is more accurate and has a superior performance over similar swarm based algorithms.

articleTitle: Depression Detection and Notification System using Image Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In today's world, the increase in academic com-petition, students face several psychological challenges such as depression, anxiety, and restlessness. If not taken care on time, it can lead to severe outcomes like suicides. Facial features and expressions can tell a lot about a person's mental health and condition. Therefore, in this paper, we aim to solve the issue to detect an early stage depression by monitoring the facial expression of students. We have also implemented an email notification system so that family can take required actions on time. Further, we have used FER2013 dataset and worked on two transfer learning models, VGG19 and ResNet50. We optimised the various parameters in the models through an iterative process of hyperparameter tuning and obtained an accuracy of 68.92% in VGG19 and 74.03% in ResNet50.

articleTitle: Eloquence in Silence: A Boon for Speech and Hearing Impaired Community
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Deaf and dumb individuals mostly utilize Eloquence in Silence to communicate with each other and within their own communities. Because they are mute, people in this language communicate with hand gestures. Eloquence in Silence Recognition is the process of identifying hand motions and carries on until equivalent hand signals are translated into text or speech. Eloquence in Silence hand motions can be categorized as either static or dynamic in this context. Though recognition of static hand gestures is easier than that of dynamic hand gestures, both types of recognition are crucial to the community of humans. By developing Deep Neural Network designs, specifically Convolutional Neural Network designs, the model can be trained to recognize hand motions. Deep Learning Computer Vision is then employed to detect and interpret hand gestures using these trained models.

articleTitle: Steer-by-Wire with Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper analyses the Steer-By-Wire (SBW) system with feedback, consisting of integral modules. It illustrates a closed loop working model, where the driver's desired steering angle is sensed and transferred to the pinion and from the pinion to the steering wheel. A cascade PI control algorithm is used for position control of the BLDC motor. The system is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink platform, to investigate the relationship between steering wheel motion and motor rotational speed, as well as the reduction of disturbances and dependable force feedback transmission to the driver steering. Also, a low-cost hardware demonstration is designed using ESP32 micro-controller.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Direct AC-AC Converter Based Wind Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a wind energy conversion system (WECS) type IV. The WECS type IV consists of the wind turbine, electric generator, alternating current-ac alternating current (AC-AC) electronic converter and the electric grid. A wind turbine emulator, a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG), and a direct matrix converter (DMC) are used for the implementation. The DMC is used to manage the power flow between the generator and the grid. On the generator side a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control, a field oriented control (FOC) and a proportional integral compensator (PI) are implemented; while on the grid side it is intended to transfer the maximum power and regulate the reactive power. Finally, the results of the WECS and its controls are shown.

articleTitle: Implementation and Analysis of SPWM and SVPWM Techniques Using STM32F407 Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Students in the electrical branch confront the various challenges of studying power electronics and their applications. The primary difficulty out of many is finding the suitable user-friendly experimental setup to implement and execute various control techniques, their functionality, and their working mechanisms. This article deals with the implementation and analysis of SPWM and SVPWM techniques in terms of output based on the fundamental voltage gained. The MATLAB Simulink-based digital simulation platform has been utilized for verification. Experimental validation is carried out by incorporating the STM32F407 microcontroller in association with the MATLAB-Waijung blockset. The outcome of this paper indicates that the results are satisfying.

articleTitle: Investigation on Digital Inverter Circuit Based on Germanium FinFET
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper investigates the behavior of the low power digital circuit for Germanium based dual stack gate-dielectrics (HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) tri-gate FinFET. To analyze the performance of the Ge based HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> dielectrics FinFET, a comparative transfer characteristic and the Transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>) are plotted for different combination of dielectric stacks as HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>. Further this proposed device is analyzed as low power digital Inverter circuit and the efficiency of the Inverter is analyzed in terms of critical Voltages as V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">IH</inf> and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">IL</inf> and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MH</inf> and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ML</inf> for different set dielectric stacks. The effects of different gate dielectrics stack on the threshold voltage (Vth) for both p and n Ge FinFET devices are also analyzed. As HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> shows better performance compared to other stack dielectrics, thus the further analysis is done on transient characteristics for different CLOAD and the output current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OUT</inf>). More interestingly, no overshoot and undershoot is present in the transient characteristics of the inverter circuit when high-k dielectric with GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is placed in stack and the effects of load capacitance (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">LOAD</inf>) on the transient characteristics show a delay in the propagation time with the increase of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">LOAD</inf>.

articleTitle: Extended Quasi-Z-Source DC-DC Converter with an Active Switched-Z-Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: On the foundation of the standard quasi-Z-source inverter, this document proposes a neoteric Z-source DC-DC converter formation for high heightens applications. Compare to enhanced-boost quasi Z-source inverter (EB-qZSI), this topology provides a smaller amount stress athwart capacitors and into the bargain, current stress across switches is impaired by half, which leads to momentous decline in conveyance losses of switches. This anticipated topology provides slightly less boost factor at low duty ratio and high modulation index at the same time as using only two L-C pairs, five diodes, one switching device and thereby plummeting the losses allied with submissive components. likewise, the proposed topology enhancements the overall efficiency of the inverter, reduces the starting inrush current problem and shares common ground between the inverter bridge and the source. The operating principle, Z-network parameters design and co-related with other impedance networks are accomplished. Finally, the simulation results for the proposed system are compared with the theoretical analysis and validated.

articleTitle: State of Charge (SOC) and State of Health (SOH) Estimation for Electric Vehicle Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The state-of-charge (SOC) and state of health (SOH) of electric car batteries within a battery management system (BMS) are both estimated comprehensively in this study article. The suggested estimating method combines state-of-the-art techniques, including an extended Kalman filter (EKF), with a model-based approach to estimate the SOC and SOH simultaneously from recorded battery voltage, current, and temperature. The EKF makes use of a battery model that accurately depicts the nonlinear and time-varying properties of the battery, allowing accurate SOC and SOH estimation even under various operating situations. The research emphasises the requirement for precise SOC and SOH estimation in electric vehicle applications and draws attention to the shortcomings of current estimation techniques. To show the potency and precision of the suggested method, simulation results are shown. The findings demonstrate that, even in the presence of varied driving profiles, temperature changes, and ageing effects, the approach provides extremely accurate SOC and SOH estimation. The proposed approach demonstrates resilience and versatility, making it ideal for actual applications involving electric vehicles. The study finds that the SOC and SOH calculation approach can considerably improve the efficiency, dependability, and longevity of the batteries used in electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Investigation of Electrical Performance for Heterojunction Vertical Tunnel FET
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This study explores the performance of silicon germanium (SiGe) vertical heterojunction tunnel FET (VTFETs) built on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) technology (SiGeVTFET) and compares it with traditional silicon-based VTFETs (Si-VTFET). The analysis, which examines several aspects such as linearity, distortion, electrical characteristics, and radiofrequency performance, is conducted using the SILVACO TCAD tool. A heterojunction is created at the source-channel interface when introducing a low-bandgap material. This shortens the tunneling path and increases the BTBT rate at which electrons tunnel. In comparison to the Si-VTFET, the SiGe-VTFET shows notable improvements, with the ONcurrent (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>) and (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf>) increasing by roughly 1.96 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> and 10.30 times, respectively. Specifically, SiGe-VTFET performs better than Si-VTFET with respect to transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>), I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> current, cut-off frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>), and transit time. These findings suggest that SiGe-VTFET holds strong promise for low-power circuit applications over its silicon-based counterpart.

articleTitle: A Reliable Routing Scheme for Vehicular AD HOC Networks using Hybrid Protocols
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANETs) play an important role in advancing road safety and traffic control through real-time data exchange. This research addresses critical challenges in VANETs, focusing on message broadcasting, link stability, and time synchronization. In the realm of message broadcasting, the first segment introduces the Reliable Message Broadcast Protocol (RMBP). RMBP leverages active Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology to enhance the accuracy of the positioning system, mitigating issues associated with GPS-based dissemination protocols. The protocol partitions the route using embedded active RFID tags, enabling location-based message broadcasting. The second segment introduces a Novel Dynamic Link Prediction Protocol (NDLP) to address the challenges posed by the dynamic nature of VANET topologies. NDLP predicts link disconnections in advance, utilizing Newton's divided difference interpolation to assess the duration of the current path's availability. By pre-emptively rerouting data packets through alternative paths, NDLP ensures uninterrupted communication. Finally, the third segment delves into the importance of precise time synchronization in large-scale VANETs. The Dynamic Message Time Synchronization (DMTS) protocol is proposed to optimize timing message coordination. DMTS employs intelligent node selection to reduce the number of transmitted timing messages, periodically readjusting clock offsets for enhanced synchronization accuracy by utilizing Maximum Likelihood estimation for clock offset design. The proposed hybrid protocols RMBP, NDLP and DMTS outperforms existing protocols in simulation analyses, demonstrating superior metrics such as delay, packet delivery ratio, and throughput in terms of reliability.

articleTitle: Control of a Parallel Robot Through Hand Movement Tracking and Gesture Recognition Employing OpenCV
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This research is enhancement of previous work and introduces a approach to control a parallel robot through hand movement tracking and gesture recognition employing OpenCV in Python, coupled with a stereo camera arrangement. The aim is to create an intuitive, gesture-driven interface enabling precise and real-time control over the robot's movements. The proposed system first employs a stereo camera setup to capture depth information and extract 3D coordinates of the user's hand movements. OpenCV facilitates real-time image processing, allowing for robust hand tracking and gesture recognition. The research findings highlight the system's robustness in accurately translating hand gestures into precise commands for controlling the parallel robot, thereby enhancing user experience and interaction efficiency. The applicability of proposed method has been presented through experimental results.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Selected Ternary Digital Circuits Based on CNTFET
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The most appropriate and effective replacement for binary logic is ternary logic. Ternary logic includes three distinct values: 0,1, and 2 and binary function has two states-logic 0,1. Ternary logic has a benefit over binary logic in that it speeds up switching. This method aids in lowering chip space, complexity. This paper analyzes the enhanced impact on both power and delay of ternary logic based on CNTFETs. Carbon nano-tube transistors are used in the creation of ternary Inverters, ternary-AND, and ternary half adder (THA) using two different approaches (with decoder-encoder approach and with decoder-less approach). Ternary logic gates that use CNTFETs have lower delays and power consumptions and ternary half adder without decoder have less power consumption when compared to Ternary Half adder with decoder.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis 6T, 8T and 10T SRAM in CMOS and FinFET Technologies: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Static Random-Access Memory (SRAM) plays a pivotal role in modern integrated circuits, serving as a critical component for data storage and fast data access. This review paper provides a comprehensive examination of SRAM cells, focusing on their implementation in two prominent semiconductor technologies: Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) and FinFET. The performance parameter analysis of the various SRAM design configurations i.e., 6T, 8T and 10T SRAM and challenges encountered in CMOS technology, highlighting key parameters such as speed, power consumption, and stability. Radiation hardness is a critical attribute for SRAM (Static Random-Access Memory) in mission-critical and radiation-prone applications due to the potential adverse effects of ionizing radiation on electronic devices like Single Event Upset (SEU) error occurring in SRAM. The resilience to radiation-induced errors is of paramount importance in the SRAM. An effort is made to compare the radiation hardness of CMOS and FinFET based SRAM architecture. This research lays emphasis on the selection of an optimal SRAM cell design, whether 6T, 8T, or 10T in CMOS or FinFET technology depends on the specific application requirements, balancing tradeoffs between area, efficiency, performance metrics, and resilience to radiation-induced faults. It also establishes the superiority of FinFET technology compared to the CMOS technology which suffers from Short Channel Effect at lower technology nodes. Further research and advancements in semiconductor technology hold the potential to refine these SRAM cell designs, addressing the evolving demands of future memory systems in both terrestrial and space environments.

articleTitle: Satellite-Based Landslide Event Detection Leveraging EfficientDet Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Timely detection and monitoring of landslides are essential for effective disaster preparedness and mitigation. With the notable advancement of remote sensing technology and the computational environment, enriched solutions are anticipated for landslide hazards. Hence this study evaluates a deep learning-driven approach for detecting landslides from satellite images. Particularly, EfficientDet, a popular single-staged object detection algorithm. A series of EfficientDet models namely D0, D1, D2, D3, and D4 are applied and implemented. For experimentation, publicly available Bijie landslide detection data is used. Furthermore, the model's performance is assessed using well-known indicators i.e., average precision and recall. The experimental results indicated that the accuracy of EfficientDet_D3 is best (AP@0.50=0.80) followed by EfficientDet_D4, EfficientDe_D1, EfficientDet_D2, EfficientDet_DO. The qualitative and the quantitative outcomes exhibit the power of deep learning algorithms in the studies of hazard analysis. Our findings contribute to proactive disaster management schemes, aiding in the growth of enhanced mitigation measures to minimize the effect of landslides on communities and the environment.

articleTitle: Non-Expansive Implementation of Discrete Wavelet Transform for Real Time Image Coding System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The filter bank implementation of standard Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) suffers from coefficient expansion problem. In this paper a methodology is proposed to address the coefficient expansion problem of standard DWT. With this methodology a non –expansive implementation is carried out without increasing computation load and memory requirements. However, this non-expansive filter bank realization of discrete wavelet transform suffers from boundary artifacts, but it is restricted to a fewer coefficients only at the boundaries. An optimal filter is required to reduce this boundary artifacts problem. The proposed non-expansive DWT is highly suited for real time wavelet based image coding system.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Algorithms Based SoH Prediction of Li-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: As the need for energy storage systems intensifies, it's becoming increasingly important to accurately predict the State of Health (SoH) of lithium-ion batteries. This is crucial for optimizing their performance, prolonging their lifespan, and ensuring reliable operation. Model-based approaches are frequently intricate and challenging to apply for complicated electrochemical systems like lithium-ion batteries, which makes data-driven estimation methods a hotspot for research. The focus of this study is to analyze and compare the predictive capabilities of feed-forward neural network (FFNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) for precise SoH estimation in lithium-ion batteries. To improve the accuracy of the models, a feature selection algorithm is used to identify the highly correlated features effecting SoH. The neural networks are then trained and tested on a comprehensive NASA battery dataset comprising selected features viz., terminal voltage, current, temperature and number of charge & discharge cycles. Novelty of this study is that the maximum error in estimating the SoH from proposed LSTM and FFNN neural network is reduced to 2.8% and 3.5% respectively. Hence, the LSTM model for SoH estimation proves to be a promising and effective approach. The potential impact of the developed SoH estimation model extends to various sectors, including electric vehicles and energy systems incorporating renewable energy, where lithium-ion battery longevity and dependability are critical.

articleTitle: Unveiling a Cutting-Edge Living Style-Based AI Model for Early Heart Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Healthcare, agriculture, cybersecurity, and finance have all become increasingly dependent on machine learning models. The advancements in machine learning have been particularly beneficial to the medical field. As long as machine-learning techniques are properly trained, they are capable of detecting numerous diseases at an early stage. By timely diagnosis and effective health management, numerous deaths arising from severe heart diseases can be prevented. This paper aims to introduce NNXBoost, a machine-learning model capable of detecting heart disease at an early stage. SMOTE is applied to balance the dataset based on an open-source dataset provided by the National Government. We then combine XGBoost with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN), utilizing the features of the neural network. Compared with other machine learning algorithms, the proposed model is evaluated based on accuracy, precision, recall, F1Score, and AUCROC metrics. A 99% accuracy rate is achieved by the suggested model, which outperforms other models. NNXBoost has the potential to contribute significantly to the field of medical science by detecting early heart disease.

articleTitle: Design of Positive Edge Triggered D Flip-Flop Using Quantum Dot Cellular Automata
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper explores the design and energy dissipation of Positive Edge Triggered D Flip-Flop at nanoscale using Quantum Dot cellular Automata (QCA) technology. QCA technology is chosen for its superior performances such as low energy consumption, high switching, less electricity leakage, small size, less heat generation, and high noise immunity. The proposed QCA based Positive Edge D Flip-Flop design aims to achieve high switching speed and reduced power consumption, which is very crucial in modern digital circuit designs. Evaluating through QCA Designer version 2.0.3, it is revealed that Proposed circuit design exhibits better performances including high switching speed and lower energy compared to traditional alternatives. These results emphasize the QCA technology's potential to develop efficient and high-performance digital circuit designs contributing low power computations and enabling various future applications across various domains. In this paper, we present a brief overview of QCA technology, circuit design and simulation of positive edge triggered D Flip-Flop using 45 QCA cells occupying an area of 0.04 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a low clock latency.

articleTitle: Toxicity Predicition of 3D-Domain Swapped Predicted Proteins using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In this study efforts are put to createimplimention of development of a structure activity relationship (SAR) based model, that is used to anticipate toxicities and save time, testing on animals, money, chemicals at the time of protein-ligand interaction for drug development. Machine learning models are implemented on seven 3D-domain swapped proteins. In first level classification model were implemented and in second level regression model were implemented. Training dataset includes swapped proteins structure with their Pharmocological activities and contain about 501 features. Because of the extreme imbalance and abundance of characteristics in our dataset, we first carried out feature selection.then the data-preprocessing. We also implemented the K-folds cross validation for the same and the simulation results were obtained.

articleTitle: A Non-Uniform Cantilever-Based Metal to Metal Contactswitch for Leakage Power Reduction in CMOS Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Downscaling of transistors over the last couple of decades has led to an increase in the leakage power in battery-functioned devices like mobile phones which consumes most of the time in standby mode. To address this issue, a comparative case study has been conducted utilizing both CMOS switches and MEMS switches. This paper focusses on the comparison of static power of CMOS circuits on employingsemiconducting switch first and then MEMS switch later. An illustration of a Half adder circuit employing CMOS logic is utilized as a case study, subsequently simulated with the integration of semiconducting switches followed by MEMS switches for comparative analysis. Upon examination of the MEMS switch characteristics, which comprised of a pull-in voltage calculated at 3.45 volts, an on-time duration of 7.45 microseconds, an off-time duration of 4.78 microseconds, and a spring constant of 0.26 N/m, there was a notable decrease in leakage power from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.22\ \mathrm{x}10^{-9}$</tex> W to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$11.23\ \mathrm{x}10^{-27}\mathrm{W}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Phishing Website Detection Using Hybrid Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper presents a machine learning model which is based on recognize phishing sites :utilizing highest model URLs and domain based features. This technique guarantees exactness without depending on outsiders. Against phishing arrangements like boycotts, whitelists, heuristics, and comparable recognition strategies can't distinguish zero-day assaults or new sites. In this paper, we present an integrated anti-phishing system that addresses recent phishing attacks in real time by stripping features from custom URLs(Uniform Resource Locator) and domain based. Phishing is famous among assailants since it is simpler to fool somebody into tapping on a pernicious connection that looks genuine than it is to get past a PC's guards. In this paper, we use an experimental method using five learning machines: Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbour, and Decision Tree, Naïve's Bayes, Logistic Regression to determine the best model for detecting phishing sites. Information is collected from legitimate sources and phishing sites. The data can be used as input for machine learning. The RF model performed better than other methods. Big data and small data are different. Target category 0 represents a legitimate website and target category 1 represents a phishing website.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Safety Through Computer Vision: A Comprehensive Approach Using Associative Rule Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Ensuring road safety is of utmost importance in contemporary urban settings, requiring creative strategies to prevent accidents and efficiently manage traffic. In this paper, we present a solution that utilizes computer vision techniques, with a specific emphasis on using associative rule mining. Our approach combines face tracking and vehicle detection using associative rule mining (ARM) to gain a comprehensive picture of traffic dynamics and improve road safety. The face tracking component enables the detection of distracted drivers or pedestrians, providing valuable information about potential safety risks. Our research adds to the expanding knowledge in the field of intelligent transportation systems by introducing a new framework that tackles the complex difficulties of road safety. This framework combines face tracking, vehicle identification, and associative rule mining to achieve its objectives. The proposed method shows potential for developing road networks that are both safer and more efficient in the age of smart cities.

articleTitle: Automated Classification of Chest CT Scans for Accurate Diagnosis and Risk Stratification: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The performance assessment metrics of the topic of classification models, such as recall, accuracy, and F1-score were considered in this work. We examined how many types of events our model categorizes well and view the more detailed metrics for every class. A special account of the precision-recall trade-off even shows that there is an undeniable advantage, and there may be a negative side. The outcomes also show how good the model is. For example, a perfect accuracy score in the 2nd Class demonstrates that the algorithm can differentiate occurrences of such a category. The weighted average metrics consider the fundamental dissimilarity in a group better. The model has an average 0.91 F1-score, indicating that it makes a balanced decision between accuracy and recall. While I can be proud of these results, I understand that the presented weaknesses realized that additional study of potential feature engineering and other model architectures remain. This experiment will be valuable for future research and usage in real-life.

articleTitle: Detection of Potato Plant Diseases Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: There is a very famous medical quote “The good- news stories in medicine are early detection, early intervention”. This applies very well in the field of agriculture as well. According to a report published in Research gate form India faces a total loss of INR 290 billion per annum. Potato crop is among the most important crop in the world. Potato crops are important because of many factors which may include benefits like Dietary Diversity, Calorific Efficiency, wide Global Acceptance etc. There are total of 30,000 plant diseases out of which 5,000 prevail in India. Potato disease such as Early Blight and Late Blight are among the diseases that leads to a huge potato crop loss in the whole world as well as India. This paper focuses on using technological advancement in the field of Computer Science as well as camera hardware capabilities to detect such plant diseases at the earliest stage which will help farmers to take appropriate measures. Some of the technologies that can be incorporated into agricultural field to detect potato plant diseases are CNN (Convolutional Neural Network), ANN (Artificial Neural Network), RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) etc.

articleTitle: Mobile-Enabled Essential Eye Checkup Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: A mobile-enabled basic eye checkup application is a promising technology that automates the assessment of eye health and visual acuity by analyzing digital eye images. This application is equipped with a deep learning model, which utilizes images to detect eye-related diseases. The application provides a series of tests that measure and evaluate the disease through visual tests and image processing, providing valuable information. Through this real-time feedback, user can perceive their eye-related data immediately. The integration of deep learning models and image processing in mobile application make it easily accessible on the go, a cost-effective and efficient solution enabling the pre-evaluation of the eye checkup.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Strategies for Effective Image Forgery Detection and Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The field of digital forensics assumes a crucial role in the investigation of digital crimes, with image forgery emerging as a critical area of concern. Delving into the intricacies of image forgery, the paper specifically addresses the challenges posed by splicing and copy/move techniques, underscoring the necessity for advanced methods in accurate localization and segmentation. Despite the existence of various techniques, per-sistent gaps remain in achieving precise forgery localization and segmentation, highlighting the imperative for robust models capable of handling diverse forgery scenarios. In this context, we propose two distinctive models where VGG19 serves as the backbone for U-Net, and ResNet acts as the backbone for LinkNet. Leveraging the inherent strengths of both convolutional architectures, the depth of VGG19 seamlessly integrates with U-Net, while ResNet's residual learning capabilities effectively meld with LinkNet, presenting a holistic approach to forgery detection. Both models are deployed to localize and segment forged regions within images. Comprehensive experimental evaluations confirm the efficiency of the suggested models when contrasted with existing techniques. Demonstrating superior performance, both models achieve notable accuracy in forgery localization and segmentation tasks. The outcomes highlight the potential impact of these models in advancing the field of digital forensics, particularly in mitigating challenges associated with splicing and copy/move attacks.

articleTitle: Common-Grounding Dual-Boost Nine-Level Inverter for Transformerless PV System
