publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Transformerless multilevel inverters (MLIs), provide grid-tied solar photovoltaic (PV) systems with a number of attractive benefits, such as increased efficiency, smaller size, and cheaper cost. They do, however, present the problem of leakage current, which needs to be resolved in order to guarantee safety and grid code compliance. A unique nine-level common-ground switched-capacitor (SC) based MLI (CG 9MLI) architecture is proposed in this paper. One source, three capacitors, nine semiconductor switches, and three diodes are employed to build the proposed circuit. Additionally, it effectively removes leakage current without compromising performance on account of the CG link. The capacitor voltages are self-balanced by the timely charging and discharging of the SCs. The suggested CG 9MLI improves cost-effectiveness and reliability by enabling effective voltage boosting with fewer components than the existing literature on transformerless MLI topologies. To confirm the viability of the inverter in both closed-loop and open-loop operating modes, simulation results are depicted.

articleTitle: Identification of Medicinal Plants for Medical Usage Using VGG16, ResNet50 and ResNet152
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The suggested study describes how to identify therapeutic plants utilizing processing approaches. The precise identification of medicinal plants is critical. The healing nature of medicinal plants, in addition to their capacity for treat a variety of ailments, necessitate the requirement for automatic identification. Different plant portions, such as the root, fruit, bark, and stem, can help with identification; however, because leaf photographs are easily accessible and provide a wealth of information, they have been widely employed. This research studies the artificial intelligence field of deep learning and proposes an ensemble learning technique for swiftly recognizing medicinal plants from leaf photos. The suggested research only focuses on the identification and categorization of distinct leaf components in order to identify the plant species. The medicinal leaf dataset has thirty categories. The approach of transfer learning was employed in our work for initializing parameters the VGG 16, ResNet50, and ResNet152 neural networks. These component models were used with the SoftMax layer to extract attributes from the input photos. The accuracy of our model is 99 in comparison to MobileNetV2-Softmax Classification and InceptionV2-softmax classification (fivefold cross-validation) is 97.49 and 98.09 respectively.

articleTitle: Rectifying the Impact of Multiple Cell Upsets in Memory Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Memories are prone to error due to neutron induced upsets. Reliable data storage hinges on the detection and correction of these errors. This work explores Multiple Cell Upsets (MCU), induced by a single event that causes adjacent bits in a continuous data stream to get corrupted simultaneously. VLSI technology with its enhanced processing capabilities, conserves seamless data integrity by embedding Error Correction Code (ECC) techniques within the memory. Divide-symbol method is employed to encode the data, and any errors that may have occurred due to MCUs will subsequently be corrected during the decoding process. This simple method is effective, as the reduced mathematical complexity ensures data integrity that is also cost-effective. The implementation of proposed technique in Xilinx Vivado, produces an improvement of 49.2% in area and 35.2% in the timing delays.

articleTitle: Current Sensorless Based Maximum Torque per Ampere Controlled Synchronous Reluctance Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In this work the Synchronous Reluctance Motor (SynRM) drive is operated under Maximum Torque/Ampere (MTPA) condition. This control strategy reduces the overall size of the machine or in other words it improves the efficiency per KW rating of the machine. This control strategy is more effective for SynRM drive for Electric Vehicle (EV) applications. To further improve its acceptability for EV applications, the drive can be made more economical by reducing the current sensors to two/one or can be totally eliminated instead of utilizing three sensors. So, from this perspective in this work the model based current estimation strategy for SynRM drive for EV applications is proposed which totally eliminates the need of current sensors for the drive. The usefulness of the proposed current estimation scheme is verified in MATLAB/SIMULINK platform.

articleTitle: Fusion of Multi-Scale CNN for Motor Imagery EEG Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) is a groundbreaking and innovative paradigm in human-computer interaction, with the potential to enhance the living standard with technological advancement. The electroencephalogram (EEG) signals associated with motor imagery (MI) have been widely employed in several BCI systems. However, the challenge of individual variability in signal patterns hinders the classifier's efficacy. This article presents a fusion multi-scale convolutional neural network (MCNN) to perform an end-to-end MI EEG classification BCI system. The proposed multi-scale CNN fusion employed spatial and depthwise filters to learn temporal and spatial MI EEG features. Multiple scales of CNN are used, since characteristics at multiple scales to develop a subject-dependent model are crucial to learn, as each individual exhibits a unique signal pattern. The evaluation for classification performance is executed using the BCI Competition IV 2a (BCIC IV 2a) dataset. Furthermore, t-SNE visualisation is shown to illustrate features extracted for a subject. Compared with some existing state-of-the-art methodologies, the proposed method demonstrates enhancements in performance metrics.

articleTitle: Implementation of Electronic Voting Machine in FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The integration of digital technology within e-Government services has underscored the pivotal role of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) in enhancing public sector efficiency and citizen participation. This paper presents a systematic exploration and implementation of an EVM employing the Register Transfer Level (RTL) methodology. The research methodology encompasses a systematic analysis of the design process involving both the Ballot Unit and Control Unit of the EVM. It delineates a four-stage design process: Initial specification, RTL Description aided by Algorithmic State Machine (ASM) charts and Finite State Machine (FSM) designs, Verilog code generation, and subsequent design verification via simulation. The voting process involves registering polled votes in individual contestant registries and validating these against registries to conclude the election process. The RTL design utilizes registers, multiplexers and adders to facilitate complex circuit synthesis with multiple states. The implementation's reprogrammability and cost-efficiency highlights its viability for electoral systems ensuring transparency, security and seamless voter engagement.

articleTitle: S2VEM: Secure Summarized Video Encryption Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: India's enormous population presents difficulties for the administration, law enforcement, and security. Because of advances in computing power and electronic storage capacity, digital videos are becoming more widespread in a variety of industries, including education and entertainment. Technology must be able to navigate through videos quickly and effectively without losing any of its content, given the growing amount of video collections. The user might not find all of the video's information important, or they might not always have the time to see it through to the end. Under these circumstances, the user might want to go through the video summary rather than watching the entire video. Watching security camera footage is a time-consuming task, as most of the time nothing happens. What if we could identify ahead of time which sequences in the security tape are relevant? While monitoring, it might save a lot of time and storage space. This research suggests an approach for securely transmitting video summaries while preserving important data through the use of strong encryption algorithms.

articleTitle: Modelling the Impact of Grain Size on Carrier Concentration & Sensitivity for Gas Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This work presents investigations on a numerical model for cylindrical and spherical shaped grains on n-type sensing film. It has been shown that modulating grain size impacts the surface potential, effective carrier concentration, and sensitivity of a metal-oxide-based gas sensor. The modeled expression presents surface potential function and effective carrier concentration in relation to surface state density for varied grain sizes of radius 2.5nm-40nm. It is observed that for smaller grain size (R< 2L) all charge particles moves from the center of grain to the surface of sensing film when excessive oxygen adsorbents interact with the sensing film. Finally, the situation of full depletion is reached and grains looks depleted of charge particles and result of it the surface potential of the sensing film rises. Further it is validated by mathematical simulations. The movement of charge particles from conduction band of film to surface state energy level (Ess) will continue till the two Fermi energy levels aligned with each other and this situation is named critical surface state density. Critical surface state density is presented for both spherical and cylindrical shape of grain sizes. The results are compared to spherical shape grains with cylindrical in terms of surface charge density, effective carrier concentration and sensitivity. For a particle size of 2.5 nm and a constant volume, the estimated value of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t,crit</inf> for cylindrical grains is 6.5*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>, whereas for spherical grains it is 8.1*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>. The value of Nt can be calculated using several values of the height of the cylindrical grain. Cylindrical grain shape shows better sensitivity in comparison with spherical grain shape.

articleTitle: Passive Image Forgery Detection Through Ensemble Learning with ELA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Today, rapid advances in science and technology have made it possible to manipulate multimedia content easily with a variety of editing tools. The integrity and trustworthiness of multimedia content are seriously threatened by this. As a result, sustaining digital images is increasingly important since they contain important information and are used as proof in a variety of sectors. A number of researchers have developed different image forensics detection methodologies due to the requirement and importance of digital image forensics. The basis of image forensics is passive image forgery detection. Passive forgeries such as image splicing, copy-move, and retouching are often used techniques that compromise the authenticity of an image. Recently, a huge amount of study has gone into creating innovative techniques for identifying various image forgeries. In this paper, we present a new methodology for detecting image forgery that accepts an RGB image as input and converts it to an error level analysis (ELA) image before classifying whether the image is tampered with or not. This model is a mix of modified DenseNet169 and modified DenseNet201. Through rigorous testing and validation, our model demonstrates a superior capacity to identify tampering even when there are realistic and subtle changes created by sophisticated image editing tools. In our investigation, we achieved an accuracy of 93.79 on test images.

articleTitle: EEG Signal Filtering Using Rectangular FIR Window Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Signal processing, audio processing, image processing, and other applications are among the numerous where data sometimes contains unwanted noise or unnecessary information. Analyses can be made clearer and more precise by filtering out or reducing noise. In data science and machine learning, filtering is a useful preprocessing technique. By eliminating outliers, superfluous features, and inconsistencies, it helps clean and prepare data for research, improving the quality of the data for further analysis or modeling. We can extract features or information from a dataset by filtering it. Filtering is critical in signal processing for extracting meaningful information from signals while eliminating noise. This is vital in many fields, including telecommunications, radar systems, and biomedical engineering, where precise signal interpretation is required. signal that can disrupt EEG. Any unintended electrical potentials in the recorded EEG are undesirable. Removing noise from EEG recordings before display allows for accurate diagnosis and interpretation. The research analysis FIR filters through the rectangular window method for filtering EEG signals which consist of different brain waves. The response time analysis for the EEG signal is calculated and also the main lobe width is calculated. The platform used for the simulation of the experiment is MATLAB2023a.

articleTitle: Solar Based Hybrid Battery Management and Online E-Bulk Station Booking System Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper introduces an intelligent and sustainable framework for Electric vehicles (EVs) that seamlessly integrates multiple features to enhance the user experience and promote eco-friendly transportation. Firstly, we detail the implementation of a solar-based hybrid battery management system, incorporating solar panels and a robust battery management system (BMS). This system intelligently manages energy flow, maximizing the utilization of renewable solar power while ensuring uninterrupted supply through efficient battery management. Secondly, we introduce an online e-bulk station booking system, facilitating efficient scheduling and utilization of EV charging infrastructure. Leveraging IoT devices, users can remotely book charging slots through a user-friendly web platform or mobile application, enhancing accessibility and convenience. Furthermore, we explore the seamless integration between the solar-based hybrid battery management system and the e-bulk station booking system. Real-time data exchange and intelligent automation optimize energy utilization, dynamically adjusting charging schedules based on solar generation, battery status, and user demand. Our proposed system addresses key challenges in renewable energy utilization and EV infrastructure management, offering a scalable and sustainable solution for future energy ecosystems. Through this interdisciplinary approach, we contribute to the advancement of renewable energy integration and smart mobility solutions.

articleTitle: Efficient Approximate Adder Design for Image Brightness Enhancement: Balancing Area, Power, and Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Adders play a fundamental role in arithmetic operations in digital circuit design, serving as the foundation for many computation activities. With the rising need for high-performance computing systems and the growth of data-intensive applications, there is a greater emphasis on improving the efficiency of adder designs. Traditional precise adders ensure accurate computation but often come at the expense of area, power consumption, and delay. This paper presents an efficient approximate Full Adder (FA) targeting area and power optimization as primary objectives. The proposed circuit is simulated using the Cadence tool with a 90nm technology node. Simulation results indicate that, on average, the proposed FA demonstrates a remarkable 41.6% reduction in area and a significant 53.3% decrease in power consumption compared to the existing efficient approximate adder IFA. These improvements are achieved through innovative circuit optimizations tailored specifically for approximate computing. Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical applicability of the proposed FA design by integrating it into an image brightness application. By leveraging the efficiency gains of the proposed FA, we achieve enhanced computational performance and reduced energy consumption in image processing tasks.

articleTitle: Smart Agriculture: Explainable Deep Learning Approach with Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In light of the pressing need to guarantee food security in the face of threats posed by climate change, an increasing global population together with rising incomes, worsening soil erosion, and dwindling water resources, crop yield forecasting has assumed more significance in recent years. A relatively new area of study, “Explainable AI” seeks to provide context for the findings produced by Deep learning models. Nevertheless, there is a pressing need for more comprehensive evaluations of deep learning models for object classification in images. Due to this, the research suggests two steps for implementing Explainable AI: (1) assessing the deep-learning(DL)-strategies accuracy utilizing evaluation methods, and (2) evaluating the feature recognition skill of an scan when recognized by DL utilizing Grad-CAM for model construal. Compared to EfficientNetV2S and Xception, the results reveal that MobieNet model has lower dependability but higher accuracy. When taking the ratio match rate into account, though, MobileNetV2 achieves the best accuracy. Building intelligent agriculture support systems (with the help of automated fruit-picking robots that discard bad fruits) is one application of the study's findings. Another is the utilization of the Explainable AI model's output to determine the best deep learning model for processing.

articleTitle: Implementation of Dual Node 12T SRAM Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In the dynamic realm of semiconductor design, the quest for improved energy efficiency and unwavering reliability propels exploration into inventive memory cell architectures. This project unveils a meticulously crafted 12T SRAM cell designed for operation in the near-threshold voltage regime, addressing soft error challenges induced by high-energy particles. Through radiation-hardened by-design principles, the innovative features of the 12T SRAM cell enhance efficiency and reliability, as validated in Cadence simulations. This research contributes valuable insights to the discourse on energy-efficient semiconductor design, marking a significant leap in reconciling the dual demands of energy efficiency and reliability in contemporary memory design for computing applications.

articleTitle: Evolving Education in India: Multilingual LLMs for Vernacular Learning Experiences
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly in the domain of natural language processing (NLP), have brought in an era of technological innovation. At the forefront of this are Large Language Models (LLMs). LLMs are neural network-based transformers trained on vast datasets. Due to their massive training data, they imbibe the intricacies of human conversation well and understand and generate human-like text. LLMs have the potential to revolutionize various sectors, with applications ranging from machine translation to sentiment analysis amongst other advanced NLP tasks. In the context of the diverse educational landscape of India, technical integration has become of the utmost importance in enhancing learning experiences and accessibility to relevant material. Amongst the many tools available to aid education, LLMs emerge as transfor-mative assets, reshaping classroom dynamics as well as bridging linguistic divides. This research explores the comprehension abilities of GPT 3.5 Turbo in Hindi, a language widely spoken across the Indian subcontinent. After use-case specific training with reading comprehension passages, a set of multiple-choice questions (MCQs) are used to assess the performance of the large language model. With a focus on vernacular languages, this study aims to impact a significant portion of the Indian student population, contributing to the availability of specialized education technology in a multilingual context.

articleTitle: Mine Blast Algorithm-Load Disturbance Rejection (MBA-LDR) Controller for Islanded Microgrid Frequency Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper aims to devise a method for identifying self-sufficient microgrids considering controllable and uncontrollable energy sources. The sources analyzed include solar, wind, and diesel generators, aqua electrolyzer, fuel cells, battery storage systems, and flywheels. Among these, solar, wind, and diesel generators, along with fuel cells, serve as power-generating sources, while Battery energy storage systems, flywheels, and aqua electrolyzer act as energy storage components. Notably, aqua electrolyzer stand out for their capability to produce hydrogen, which is then used as fuel for fuel cells. The paper addresses challenges arising from load and source variations, leading to frequency deviations within the system. To counteract these deviations and maintain system frequency, the paper suggests employing Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller. This controller regulates the output power of diesel generators, fuel cells, battery storage systems, flywheels, and aqua electrolyzer and loads. Additionally, Load Distribution Rejection (LDR) techniques employed to fine-tune the gains of the hybrid system. The paper evaluates system responses using classical, LDR, and Mine blast Algorithm (MBA) based LDR methods, demonstrating the superior performance of the MBA-LDR controller in terms of settling time, number of oscillations, and peak deviations.

articleTitle: WellnessWizz – Conversation AI for Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: WellnessWizz is an advanced healthcare platform that improves early diagnosis and risk assessment for breast cancer and polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) by utilizing chatbots and machine learning algorithms. People can share details about their symptoms and risk factors with chatbots via an easy-to-use interface. WellnessWizz uses an advanced Decision Tree Classifier to precisely detect possible PCOS instances and assess the risk of breast cancer based on its analysis of this data. The goal of this project is to provide individuals with personalized, real-time assessments, hence boosting healthcare efficiency and accessibility. This project highlights the potential of technology-driven solutions to promote proactive healthcare management by seamlessly integrating cutting-edge technologies. The platform enables early intervention strategies, thereby improving the health of women suffering from these common but commonly misdiagnosed conditions all across the world. The chatbot represents a significant step forward in utilizing artificial intelligence and machine learning to address critical healthcare challenges, paving the way for more innovative and impactful solutions in the future.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Sensor-Based Trapezoidal Control of BLDC Motor Based on XMC-7200 Microcontroller for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Nowadays with the exponential growth in technology efficiency is a very critical aspect of any electrical drive system. Using BLDC motors in place of conventional AC induction motors and brushed DC motors can improve efficiency and save energy. In this paper implementation of speed control of brushless DC motor using hall effect sensors with PI controller using XMC 7200 MCU for electric vehicle-type application has been proposed. Block commutation or six-step commutation or trapezoidal control technique is used for the commutation of the phases. This method is straightforward and cost-effective from the implementation of a hardware point of view. A simulation study and hardware implementation have been carried out for this scheme.

articleTitle: Video Summarization using Bidirectional RNN and Vanilla Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Video summarization aims to select the most rele-vant and important segments of a video to compose a summary. In this study, a novel approach is introduced to evaluate frame importance for effective summarization through the comprehension of video temporal and spatial arrangements. The archi-tecture employs a vanilla autoencoder and Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks (Bi-RNNs), augmented with an attention mechanism to highlight pertinent frames. An enhancement over recent state-of-the-art methods is achieved on the widely used SumMe dataset, with a notable increase of 3% in F1-scores compared to supervised learning techniques and 5% compared to unsupervised learning methods.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-Assisted Deep Neural Network Design for Multiple Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The generation of vast amounts of data, coupled with significant advancements in computational platforms, offers numerous opportunities for a wide range of classification tasks across various applications. These classifications have been made possible by successful research in deep learning (DL) methodologies over the past decade, which have progressively matured and achieved human-level accuracy. Healthcare applications are a major segment where DL algorithms with transfer learning have tremendous opportunities for different tasks viz. test diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies. In this paper transfer learning-assisted deep neural network design and Deep Learning Processor Unit-based hardware implementation for multiple healthcare applications is presented. Experimental results indicate that the proposed methodology can enable different state-of-the-art model implementations to achieve significant accuracies of 95.2%, 98.5%, and 98.2%, and frame rates of 498.24, 546.89, and 368.24 FPS (frames per second) on different benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Understanding Thermal Performance of Vernacular Houses for Propagating Sustainable Energy Techniques in Design and Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Indigenous and vernacular houses have always provided conducive thermal indoors irrespective of harsh outdoor climatic conditions. This time-tested technology has in modern context paved the way for a sustainable yet energy efficient way for maintaining a thermal conducive environment inside. The present study investigates the relationship between indoor-outdoor thermal environment parameters, personal adaptations and involved design-planning and construction techniques for three different styled houses for a composite climate. A thermal performance study of 30 houses each of vernacular, additive vernacular, and contemporary style based on field measurements, and the questionnaire-based survey was done. Physical and personal variables were recorded using ASHRAE's seven-point and Nicole's five-point scale. ASHRAE(55/2010) standard was used to ascertain comfort temperatures and identify thermal comfort strategies. Analysis showed wide variations in indoor thermal comfort temperatures with comfort range varying from 21-24°C for vernacular houses, as against 20-25°C for additive and 17-30°C for contemporary modern houses with corresponding neutral temperatures. Results showcased better thermal performance of vernacular houses than contemporary modern houses owing to traditional materials and design-planning techniques. It provides a way in which traditional architectural features and materials can be incorporated into modern houses to improve the energy performance of modern buildings in a sustainable manner.

articleTitle: Determination of the Energy Use Pattern of Residential Buildings using Survey Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The paper presents a detailed methodology to determine the energy use pattern of residential buildings along with its breakup in different processes such as heating, cooling, refrigeration, lighting, ventilation, etc. Classification of residential buildings has been done using primary and secondary data and the further sample size is determined using the Number of stories and families per household The data on the use of appliances from sample houses are collected for September, December, March, and June and are validated through energy meter readings obtained from the supplier. It has been found that the energy consumption pattern is a result of the number & character of appliances, usage of the appliances, and occupancy of a household, but the variation in the energy consumption is a result of various physical factors of the building, socioeconomic factors of the household, and appliance star rating.

articleTitle: A Review of Micro-Hydro System Topologies Operating at Off-Grid Locations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Micro hydro plants at off-grid locations are considered far more beneficial than the centralized grid extended plant at isolated locations in terms of capital investment and sustainability. To achieve control over voltage and frequency, many schemes were developed including dumping of the generated active power in auxiliary loads present in electronic load controllers. The proposal of utilizing this discarded power was worth analyzing. Methods like using storage system in micro hydro provided plenty of options making use of this wasted power. Also, modifications in the Electronic Load Controller (ELC) corresponding to the load configuration proved to be beneficial in one or the other way with various concepts to improve the efficiency of the system. The motive of this paper is to discuss the advancements brought in past or are to be brought in future in the decentralized micro hydro plants. We have presented the voltage and frequency control (VFC) of micro hydro with the merits and demerits of all the methods discussed thoroughly.

articleTitle: A Cybercrime Detection and Mitigation Framework for Online Credit Card Frauds
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The word “cybercrime” refers to any illegal behavior that is carried out with the use of computing devices, smartphones, desktops, and laptops via the Internet. This includes any type of activity that comes under “computer crime.” The scope of these crimes and the damage they cause can vary widely, and they frequently take advantage of flaws in computer systems. Cybercrime is a massive and rapidly growing problem that can have significant ramifications not only for individuals but also for businesses, including monetary, legal, and personal problems. Money, happiness, and ideology are some of their sinister objectives. It could devastate individuals, companies, and society. These effects range from human injury and national security threats to monetary damages and damage to reputation. Law enforcement, cybersecurity specialists, and policymakers must comprehend cybercrime's causes to develop effective prevention and prosecution strategies. Cybercrime prevention must involve individuals, companies, governments, and regulatory authorities. The fight against cybercrime is an ongoing process that calls for constant vigilance and the ability to react to new dangers quickly. In this paper, we propose a cybercrime mitigation framework. We also discuss the motivation behind online criminal activity. Further, the devastating effects of cybercrimes are discussed. Further, the conjoin of cybercrimes and social security is provided. Finally, some of the future research directions related to cybercrime mitigation framework are given.

articleTitle: Modelling Analysis of SEPIC and ZETA Converter Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The paper provides a thorough examination and comparison of Single-Ended Primary-Inductor Converter (SEPIC) and Zeta converter topologies in open and closed-loop setups. The study commences by outlining the design and simulation of each converter in an open-loop state, utilizing the provided schematics and simulation findings as a foundation for debate. Each converter's open-loop behavior is assessed, focusing on the early transient reactions and steady-state performances. Moreover, closed-loop control implementation is investigated to improve the stability and dependability of each system when dealing with different load circumstances. The research contrasts the two topologies based on efficiency, voltage conversion ratio, ripple characteristics, and transient response. The text includes a discussion on the appropriateness of each converter for various applications, offering significant guidance for power electronics engineers in choosing the right converter architecture for specific scenarios. The examination ends with suggestions for future research and possible enhancements in converter design.

articleTitle: Mortality Risk Prediction in Patients After Cardiac Surgery Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Norwood surgery restores systemic flow in neonates with solitary ventricle inherited heart abnormalities, but it is complicated and deadly. We created machinelearning(ML) strategies to anticipate cardiac surgery mortality using preoperative and intraoperative risk indicators. Mortality after surgery was the main consequence. Sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and AUC were used to estimate model performance. The visualization algorithm used Shapley's additive explanations. Random-forest, neural-network, SVM, and gradient-boosting had AUC-values of 0.87, 0.79, 0.81, and 0.82 for anticipating cardiac surgery operative mortality, while EuroSCORE I and II, STS, and LR had 0.70, 0.73, 0.71, and 0.74. Shapley's additive explanations study of RF identified the top-20 predictors and individual-level explanations. ML strategies based on clinical data may anticpate heart surgery postoperative mortality better than clinical grading methods. Explanatory models can account for affecting factors to provide tailored risk profiles. These machine learning-driven models need more prospective multicenter studies to prove their therapeutic efficacy.

Index Terms: Intensive Care Unit Length Of Stay

articleTitle: Streamlined U-Net for MRI Brain Tumor Segmentation with Streamlit Visualization Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Brain tumor segmentation from MRI scans is a critical process in medical diagnostics, influencing both the prognosis and the strategy of treatment for patients. Traditional methods of segmentation by radiologists are not only time-intensive but also prone to human error, necessitating the development of automated and precise segmentation techniques. This research introduces an optimized U-Net convolutional neural network architecture specifically adapted for the segmentation of brain tumors from MRI data. The proposed model is designed to enhance segmentation accuracy and is trained extensively on a diverse dataset with meticulous augmentation to ensure robust generalizability. Alongside the algorithmic contributions, this study also presents an interactive visualization tool developed using streamlit, which enables clinicians to dynamically interact with both the raw and processed MRI data. The interface boasts real-time segmentation capabilities, thereby providing an accessible platform for medical professionals to validate and utilize the segmentation output. The model is better at accurately drawing the edges of tumors, as shown by the results of the experiments. This shows that it could be used in clinical settings and is an improvement over current segmentation methods. The research encapsulates not only a methodological innovation in medical imaging analysis, but also a step forward in the practical utility of such technologies in a clinical environment.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Diagnosis of Multi-Class Open-Circuit Switch Faults in Three-Phase Front-End Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper analyzes the application of benchmark classification techniques for multi-class diagnosis of open-circuit switch faults (OCSFs) in three-phase front-end converters (TP-FECs). OCSFs result in harmonic distortion, secondary faults, and unscheduled shutdowns in power utilities. Moreover, due to the inherent difference between OCSFs and short-circuit switch faults, the same diagnosis techniques do not apply to both types of faults. This paper presents a detailed study on a two-level TP-FEC to generate single-, double-, and triple-switch OCSFs, resembling real-world scenarios. The single-moment fault data with 624 observations is captured through 13 distinct features to extract the fault characteristics during each of the 38 classes of OCSFs under varying load demands. Later, the paper analyzes the performance of neural networks (NNs), support vector machines (SVMs), ensemble bagged trees (EBTs), and k-nearest neighbours (KNNs) for multi-class diagnosis of OCSFs. The evaluation employed cross-validation with optimal hyperparameter combinations to train different models. Through rigorous experiments, we demonstrate the superiority of NNs in classifying multi-class OCSFs with a testing accuracy of 97.50%, achieving an improvement of 0.4%, 2.4%, and 3.8% compared to SVM, KNN, and EBT, respectively. Furthermore, our experiments underscore the efficacy of NNs and SVMs over other state-of-the-art methods for diagnosing OCSFs.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Method for Optimal Route Calculation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This study unveils an innovative approach to optimizing routes by merging the capabilities of the BellmanFord algorithm with the adaptive nature of Q-Learning, addressing the dynamic obstacles encountered in route planning. By integrating the Bellman-Ford algorithm, renowned for its shortest path calculation even with negative weights, with the dynamic adaptability offered by Q-Learning, we introduce a method that surpasses the limitations of traditional routing strategies. Through a series of simulations, our proposed methodology showcases enhanced adaptability, efficiency, and precision in navigating dynamic environments, outperforming both conventional routing strategies and standalone machine learning approaches. The collaboration between Bellman-Ford and Q-Learning yields a robust solution for real-time routing challenges, making it indispensable for applications in logistics, autonomous vehicle navigation, and efficient traffic management. This contribution signifies a groundbreaking step in the domain of route optimization, offering a model that proficiently adjusts to evolving conditions, thus leading the way for future research and applications in this field.

articleTitle: Securing Banking Applications in the Cloud: Challenges and Strategies for Enhanced Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: As the banking sector embraces virtual transformation, cloud computing gives a myriad of advantages such as scalability, agility, and cost-efficiency. However, the migration of banking applications to the cloud introduces precise protection demanding situations that must be addressed to guard sensitive financial information and ensure regulatory compliance. This studies paper examines the precise security worries related to deploying banking programs within the cloud and explores techniques and best practices for mitigating risks and improving security position. Through a complete evaluation of existing literature, case studies, and regulatory frameworks, this paper provides insights into the evolving landscape of cloud structures safety in banking programs and offers steering for banking institutions to navigate this paradigm shift securely.

articleTitle: Graph Convolution Network with Temporal Features for Autism Disorder Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a significant developmental brain disorder. Recently, several advanced deep learning techniques leveraging functional magnetic resonance imaging (FMRI) data have emerged for ASD classification. Notably, graph neural networks, extending deep neural network models to graph-structured data, have demonstrated considerable benefits. Various GNN models have been proposed in the past, including the latest Heterogeneous Graph Convolution Attention Network (HCAN), which combines the phenotype features of patients and generates a graph. While some studies make use of temporal features in FMRI data, few integrate these features with phenotype data. This study presents a novel approach by adapting the state-of-the-art HCAN architecture to incorporate temporal features. By merging these two methodologies, the research seeks to propel the field towards improved accuracy and reliability in ASD detection.

articleTitle: Metaheuristic Optimization Techniques for Economic Dispatch in Power Generation: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Optimizing Combined Heat and Power Economic Dispatch (CHPED) presents a multifaceted challenge to minimize operational costs while navigating various operational and power network constraints. It considers valve-point loading, transmission losses, generation capacity limits, and heat-power dependencies. Traditional and experience-based optimization algorithms address these challenges. This paper reviews heuristic optimization's application in CHPED, exploring popular methods and their implementation. It analyzes contributions, focusing on equality and inequality constraints. This study evaluates optimization techniques, comparing convergence speed, solutions, and constraints. Optimal solutions for operational costs are presented using various optimization methods.

Author Keywords: Combined heat and power economic dispatch (CHPED)

articleTitle: Masked Face Detection and Reconstruction for Identity Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of face masks as a protective measure in response to global health concerns, the landscape of facial recognition and identity verification systems faces new challenges. This research paper delves into the development of advanced techniques for the detection of masked faces and the subsequent reconstruction of facial features to enhance identity verification accuracy. The proposed methodology leverages state-of-the-art computer vision algorithms to identify and localize masked faces in images and video streams. By addressing the unique challenges posed by obscured facial features, the system employs deep learning models trained on diverse datasets, encompassing a variety of mask types, facial expressions, and lighting conditions. Furthermore, this research introduces a novel approach for facial feature reconstruction where this paper classifies the gender of the masked face using Inceptionv3 and gets an accuracy of 87.5%, after segmenting of the edges is done by using YOLOv8 and an accuracy of 92.3%, and for generating the facial features of the segmented areas this paper uses Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP), aiming to restore essential identity-related information of the individual wearing face mask. The reconstruction process employs generative models and facial landmark localization for predicting and regeneration of obstructed facial attributes, thereby helping to improve identity verification performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power Quality in Distribution System with DVR, D-SATCOM and UPQC Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The power generated by electricity industry is presently concentrating on the mitigation of power quality (PQ) difficulties. Numerous PQ issues are brought about by automation in industry and the integration of distributed generation using power electronic converters. This calls for PQ enhancement, This contributes to the equipment's extended lifespan and increase dependability of supplies for feeding vital loads into the system. Electric power transmission efficiency from the source to industrial, home, and commercial consumers is measured by power quality. Voltage quality is a factor in at least 50% of issues with power quality. An improved power quality is presented in this paper. using Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC), distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM), Dynamic Voltage Restorers (DVR). The UPQC is a member of the active power filter family. It helps with power factor adjustment, integrating energy from renewable sources systems into the distribution network, and resolving source PQ problems relating to voltage and current. By integrating DVRs with D-STATCOM, UPQC is a significant multifunctional FACTS device that helps reduce the results of unbalanced loads, harmonic currents, and voltage sags and swellings. Using MATLAB/SIMULINK software, a simulation investigation of the suggested topology was conducted. The findings are reported.

articleTitle: DonorHarbor: Orchestrating Organ Giving with Centralized Wallet Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Addressing the pressing issue of organ shortages for transplantation is paramount, as countless families endure the agonizing wait for suitable donors. Current obstacles, including a limited donor pool and convoluted intermediary processes, impede progress in organ allocation. This paper proposes a decentralized web application, leveraging the transparency, privacy, and decentralization features of blockchain technology to streamline communication among hospitals, organ recipients, and potential donors. The innovative design ensures user-friendly interaction with blockchain-based smart contracts, eliminating concerns about key management and ensuring security. This approach significantly improves transaction traceability and eliminates the need for cumbersome middleman networks, addressing key healthcare industry issues. Importantly, the economic efficiency of this system empowers patients to navigate transplantation without incurring exorbitant costs, providing a promising solution to a pressing healthcare challenge. DonorHarbor represents a promising solution to the organ shortage crisis, offering hope to those in need of life-saving transplants.

articleTitle: Simplifying Image Captioning in Hindi with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: We aim to simplify and optimize the process of generating Hindi captions for visual content using deep learning models. With the advancements in deep learning, generating textual descriptions for images is now possible. Any spelling, grammar, and punctuation errors have been corrected. However, extending this capability to languages other than English presents notable challenges. To bridge this gap, we propose a streamlined approach for generating image captions in Hindi. Our proposed methodology utilizes a neural network model that employs a multilayered CNN-LSTM architecture with attention mechanisms to enhance caption generation. The model has been trained on a dataset that has been sourced from MSCOCO and we have adapted and optimized hyper parameters to increase the probability of generating accurate Hindi descriptions. To evaluate the effectiveness of our models, we use BLEU scores that demonstrate significant improvements compared to existing work in this domain. Our research holds great significance beyond just technological innovation. We acknowledge the potential impact of automatic description of events in the environment and their translation into captions or messages on society. By simplifying the image captioning process in Hindi, we aim to promote linguistic inclusivity and provide a convenient interface for Hindi speakers, encouraging them to engage more easily with the diverse digital landscape. As we embark on this journey, our dedication goes beyond the intricacies of deep learning. Our goal is to simplify and make the process of generating image captions accessible and effective for the Hindi-speaking community. This research is in line with the wider discussion on linguistic diversity, cultural relevance, and the democratization of digital experiences in the ever-changing landscape of language technology.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Driven Decentralized Healthcare Data Management with IPFS and Elasticsearch
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In response to the pressing challenges of security, transparency, and interoperability in healthcare data manage-ment, the proposed model emerges as a pioneering solution. This paper introduces a decentralized ecosystem, powered by blockchain, IPFS, and Elasticsearch, aimed at transforming the conventional healthcare data paradigm. Traditional systems often struggle with security concerns and lack transparency in data transactions. The proposed system addresses this gap by employing a permissioned blockchain, ensuring tamper-proof patient records. Leveraging IPFS for decentralized storage and Elasticsearch for real-time data retrieval, the platform offers a resilient and efficient solution. The significance of the proposed system lies in its user-centric design, enabling patients to manage their data securely and providing healthcare providers with swift, real-time access to critical information. This research highlights the project's novel approach, emphasizing enhanced security, transparent data transactions, and improved accessibility. The proposed system acts as a pioneer in rethinking healthcare data management, introducing a solution that harmoniously integrates with the continuously evolving demands of the digital healthcare landscape. As we navigate the complexities of modern healthcare, the proposed system heralds a new era, introducing innovative methodologies that elevate the standards of security, trans-parency, and interoperability in healthcare data management.

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy Storage System: A Review of Strategies and Topologies in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs), powered by electric motors and rechargeable batteries, are revolutionizing transportation. Hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) utilize energy recuperation during braking to enhance range and fuel efficiency. Meeting the demands of varying operational conditions necessitates innovative energy storage solutions. High-power-density ultracapacitors (UCs) are pivotal in HEVs, particularly during acceleration, alleviating peak power demands on batteries. This enhances performance, prolongs battery life, and extends travel range. The EV domain offers a spectrum of energy storage options including supercapacitors (SCs), batteries, fuel cells (FCs), and UCs. Hybrid Energy Storage Systems (HESS), combining UCs and Lithium-Ion batteries, offer robust energy management capabilities. During intense braking, UCs efficiently capture and store excess kinetic energy, transferring it to the battery at peak charge levels. This seamless transition between dissipative elements and storage components optimizes system efficiency. This comprehensive review aims to validate HESS efficacy through comprehensive modeling of battery, UC, and DC motor dynamics. It explores HESS applications, interconnection strategies, and energy management principles, analyzing various topologies to enhance EV performance and sustainability.

articleTitle: Bridging Hardware and Software: A Holistic Approach to Home Automation via IOT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a transformative paradigm, revolutionizing various aspects of modern life, including residential living. As the world becomes increasingly interconnected, the integration of IoT technologies into home automation systems holds immense relevance in optimizing comfort, efficiency, and security within households. This research paper explores the significance of IoT in the context of a home automation project leveraging a Node MCU-Flask-React architecture. In today's fast-paced world, the demand for smart solutions that streamline daily tasks and enhance quality of life is ever-growing. IoT-based home automation offers a compelling solution by enabling remote control and monitoring of household devices through interconnected systems. The project described herein exemplifies the practical application of IoT principles, demonstrating how hardware and software can seamlessly collaborate to create intelligent environments tailored to individual preferences. The relevance of IoT in home automation extends beyond mere convenience; it encompasses broader implications for energy conservation, safety, and resource optimization. By integrating sensors, actuators, and data analytics capabilities, IoT-enabled systems can intelligently adapt to user behavior, optimize energy consumption, and enhance home security protocols. Such advancements are crucial in addressing contemporary challenges related to energy sustainability and urban living. Moreover, the proposed project underscores the utilization of smart technologies, making advanced automation capabilities accessible to a broader audience. By leveraging open-source frameworks like Node MCU, Flask, and React, the barriers to entry for developing and deploying IoT solutions are significantly reduced, fostering innovation and collaboration in the field. This research paper highlights the profound relevance of IoT in reshaping residential living experiences. it elucidates how IoT technologies can empower individuals to create smarter, more efficient homes tailored to their unique needs. As society progresses towards a more connected future, the integration of IoT into everyday life will continue to redefine the way we interact with our living spaces, driving towards a more sustainable and intelligent future.

articleTitle: The State-of-the-Art Techniques of Artificial Intelligence for Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The Smart Grid represents a new paradigm for electricity generation and distribution. Shifting from the traditional power grid to this innovative system will provide better management of energy demands and address other issues in the power sector. We explore various domains of this paradigm to provide insight into the topic, discussing major issues that arise during the transition. The application of Artificial Intelligence is already proving its impact on different challenges within the Smart Grid and can be further implemented for other existing problems. We discuss various methods to improve its performance, presenting AI techniques that can handle numerous issues. Future directions for each concern are also presented.

articleTitle: Free Space Optical communication for Tactical Environment: Potential Applications, Challenges and Mitigation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Free Space Optical (FSO) Communication technology is gaining momentum as a robust, swift, and secure option for broadband communication. By utilizing free space as its medium, FSO offers advantages such as high reliability, fast data transfer rates, and enhanced security, making it an attractive choice for both civilian and military applications. Researchers are actively exploring its potential in various domains due to its numerous benefits, including rapid deployment, absence of the need for licensed spectrum, cost-effectiveness, and simplicity of design compared to traditional Radio Frequency (RF) systems. In tactical environment, FSO can significantly improve communication capabilities, enabling faster and more secure transmission of critical data for battlefield surveillance, operations, and command/control systems. Its resilience against interference and jamming makes it particularly appealing for secure communications in hostile environments. However, challenges like atmospheric turbulence and line-of-sight interruptions pose significant hurdle to fully exploit the capability of FSO for communication grade availability of the link. This paper explores FSO's promise in enhancing communication in tactical environments along with effective strategies to overcome its challenges, facilitating its implementation in military and defense operations. The paper also identifies the research needs on FSO system in Indian weather context.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Asymmetric Link-Based AODV Routing Protocol for Low Power and Lossy Networks in COOJA Simulator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Route discovery for Point-to-Point (P2P) traffic flows is critical in Low-power and Lossy Networks (LLNs), especially in home and building automation applications. Although the Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks (RPL), standardized by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), is widely used, it struggles to efficiently handle P2P flows, leading to congestion at the Destination Oriented Directed Acyclic Graph (DODAG) root and increased packet delays. The P2P-RPL protocol aims to address this issue, but neither RPL nor P2P-RPL adequately account for asymmetric wireless links in their route computations. AODV-RPL, a protocol draft adopted by the IETF's ROLL working group, offers a reactive P2P route discovery mechanism based on Ad Hoc On-demand Distance Vector Routing (AODV), operating with RPL in its storing mode. This study assesses the performance of AODV-RPL using the Cooja simulator across various network topologies and node densities, considering both symmetric and asymmetric links. Through extensive simulations, it is demonstrated that AODV-RPL outperforms traditional RPL in Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) and delay performance for numerous source and destination pairs. However, while AODV-RPL generally improves upon traditional RPL for P2P routes, some node pairs remain where the difference in relative hop distance is minimal.

articleTitle: Multimode Adaptive Control Implementation for Solar PV Based EV Charging System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Efficient and sustainable charging infrastructure is critical for widespread electric vehicle (EV) adoption. To address challenges in developing sustainable and efficient EV charging infrastructure, this paper presents a novel approach: a solar PV-based charging system integrated with a Logarithmic Normalized Least Mean Square (LNLMS) adaptive control algorithm. LNLMS overcomes limitations of existing method by offering faster convergence, lower error, and DC offset rejection, enabling optimal power extraction from solar panels, efficient EV charging, and seamless grid integration while maintaining voltage stability and minimizing harmonic distortion. The paper details the proposed system, implementation, and performance evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving sustainable and efficient EV charging, grid compliance, and improved power quality. Simulation results are analyzed under different transient modes to verify the suitable V2G and G2V operations.

articleTitle: A Bone Metastatic Cancer Origin Prediction Using Deep Learning on Digital Pathological
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The key to effective treatment for bone cancers is a precise imaging diagnosis. The diagnosis process might be improved with the introduction of AI and machine-learning(ML) techniques for characterizing and evaluating bone tumors on different imaging modalities. When it comes to clinical treatments, knowing where bone metastasis cancer (OBMC) originated is crucial. With little clinical data and bone biopsy, OBMC determination is difficult for pathologists. In order to forecast the OBMC from hematoxylineosin (H&E) stained slides alone, we developed a regional multiple-instance learning algorithms. We trained the model with data from 1041 instances across 8 institutions and 26,431 areas of interest that were tagged. External validation and ten-fold cross validation were used to evaluate the model's performance. Using top3 predictions as a guide, we ran an IHC test on 175cases with unclear origins to see how well the model's predictions matched up with the results shown by the markers. We also used the model to determine if a tumor was present in a specific area and to differentiate between neuroendocrine tumors, squamous cell carcinoma, and adenocarcinoma. With a 98.98% success rate in tumor detection and a 93.85% success rate in differentiating between three cancer kinds, the suggested model was a clear winner. Our model showed promise in assisting pathologists in accurately diagnosing the OBMC and performed well when used to predict the OBMC from standard histology.

articleTitle: Cross-Lingual Text Categorization Using Social Media Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This article delves into the issues regarding cross-lingual methods for text categorization and sentiment analysis tasks using multilingual social media data. Sentiment analysis ascertains the subjective thoughts or sentiments stated, whereas text categorization automatically applies predefined categories to text. Effective cross-lingual strategies that may transmit knowledge across languages are essential given the popularity of user-generated content on social media platforms that are produced in a variety of languages. We assess the effectiveness of various transfer learning techniques, such as machine translation, cross-lingual word embeddings, and recent developments in multilingual language models, using benchmark datasets spanning multiple language corpus pairs like English-Hindi, English-Telegu) for sentiment analysis and text categorization. Our experiments reveal insights into the strengths and limitations of different cross-lingual transfer approaches. Our results showed the advantages and disadvantages of various cross-lingual transfer strategies. We investigated data augmentation by translation to enhance efficiency for languages with limited resources. The findings have consequences for commercial and research activities in this domain and lead to the development of strong cross-lingual content analysis algorithms for the multilingual social media landscape.

articleTitle: Eye Contact During Live Video Conferencing Using External Video Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Video conferencing and other forms of live communication methods enjoy widespread popularity. However, the absence of interpersonal, psychological, or tactile feedback diminishes engagement compared to in-person communication. A notable challenge arising from the distance between the webcam and display of the device lies in the absence of contact of eye during live video conferences. Addressing this issue involves manipulating video frames to alter the direction of the gaze, creating the illusion of sustained eye contact. This research introduces a technique for preserving eye contact, entailing the rotation of a user's eyeball prior to transmitting the frame of video to the distant place. The implementation leverages WebRTC and TFLite within a application optimized for mobile devices. Convolutional neural networks based on warping play a pivotal role in superimposing the corrected eye onto the detected eye position during the eye position correction process. The employed loss functions contribute to maintaining the geometry of the eye structures while mitigating color shifts around the borders of the eye regions. The technology's real-time eye gaze rectification capability on consumer-oriented mobile devices is demonstrated, highlighting its remarkable speed and resolution. This approach to gaze correction, achieved through postprocessing, proves to be a practical solution for addressing the challenge of lost contact of eye during real time video communication. The model's integration into an application facilitates its implementation.

articleTitle: Analyzing RSA and Paillier Encryption Schemes: Secure Multiplication in Homomorphic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Homomorphic encryption stands as a cornerstone in modern cryptography, facilitating computations on encrypted data while safeguarding privacy. Within this realm, RSA (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman) and Paillier encryption are notable schemes. RSA encryption, leveraging the challenge of factoring large prime numbers, supports Homomorphic operations but grapples with computational overhead in multiplication tasks. In contrast, Paillier encryption simplifies multiplication by transforming it into addition. A comprehensive comparative analysis between RSA and Paillier encryption underscores their distinct advan-tages. While RSA encryption boasts widespread adoption and robustness, Paillier encryption excels in efficiency and security for homomorphic multiplication operations. However, the choice between the two hinges on specific application requirements. Balancing factors such as computational complexity, security guarantees, and practical considerations becomes imperative. Ultimately, selecting the most suitable encryption scheme en-tails a thorough assessment of these factors to ensure optimal performance and security in the given context.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Sign Language Gesture Recognition with Multilingual Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The new developments and recent research in the field of machine translation and image captioning have enhanced the job of translation using machines. Sign language which has been a barrier in communication has successfully included itself as a maj or language. Sign language translation to and from becomes of utmost importance and image captioning helps the cause. The project includes various models including YOLOv5, LSTM-GRU and random forest with libraries like OpenCV and frameworks like MediaPipe to attain the required goal. Machine translation is done in multiple languages namely English, Hindi and French. Machine Translation is attained through a combination of different tokenizers, optimizers and models like auto-tokenizer, Adam optimizer and LSTM respectively. This project would not only help bridge the gap of communication eradicating the language barriers but also help in efficient communication with visually impaired people using text to speech and also with the auditory impaired individuals by text-to-speech and also using image recognition to understand sign language eradicating almost all the barriers that are present in verbal communication with the impaired. To create such a model, an individual needs to understand the scope of the system and also the requirements and a proper understanding of the entire procedure which accumulates into building an efficient system that suits every basic requirement of the user and also the goals the system is set to achieve.

articleTitle: Multi-Lingual Semantic-Based Sentiment Analysis Using Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Generative AI models have extensive applications in Natural Language Processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs) across various domains. They demonstrate high performance in numerous NLP tasks such as summarization, language understanding, reasoning, language generation, question-answering, sentiment categorization, and translation. Newer LLMs are projected to analyse and generate text in multiple languages because to their training on multilingual datasets, like ChatGPT, BLOOMZ, and other similar versions. Considering how frequently LLMs are used, it is critical to assess their effectiveness in multilingual environments. A major issue to be noted is that in a zero-shot context, the present generative models are not very good at producing text in Indian languages. Several scholarly articles studied generative LLMs in the English language. In contrast, LLM for Indic languages is not meant to be used in a zero-shot manner in downstream applications due to poor generating performance. Generative LLMs evaluate models on standard NLP benchmarks covering NLP datasets in diverse languages. We compared the performance of generative LLMs with non-autoregressive models on these tasks to evaluate the generative AI model's performance compared to the previous generation of LLMs. A framework for evaluating generative LLMs in the multilingual setting has been evaluated to provide future directions.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Object Detection Algorithms for Autonomous Parking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In response to the challenges posed by increasing urbanization, traditional parking systems face numerous issues, such as inaccurate slot detection and manual tracking, which exacerbate traffic congestion and environmental strain. This paper presents an autonomous parking system as a solution to these challenges. By leveraging advanced object detection algorithms, including YOLO-NAS, YOLOv8, and DETR models, this system revolutionizes parking space identification, freeing drivers from the task of manual searching. Our research focused on identifying the most suitable object detection algorithm for our dataset and objectives. Utilizing the ‘PKLot’ Dataset, we trained and fine-tuned our models, ensuring consistency in hyperparameters across algorithms to isolate their impact on performance. We evaluated algorithmic efficacy using metrics like mean average precision (mAP) and latency, measuring accuracy in discerning occupied and vacant spaces alongside real-time processing efficiency. Our evaluation results highlight the performance differences among algorithms, guiding future research. This research advocates for an intelligent, autonomous approach to parking management, aligning with goals of optimizing operations and promoting sustainable urban development.

articleTitle: Impacts of Cyber Attack on Performance of Current-Based Relays in Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Cyber-attacks can interfere with digital protection relays, modifying their command outputs to circuit breakers. This study aims to present monitoring methods for current-based relays under the threat of cyber-attacks, with a focus on overcurrent and current differential relays. These relays are valued for their fast, sensitive, selective, and secure operation. However, their susceptibility to cyber intrusions poses significant challenges to the reliability and security of power grids. The research employs a comprehensive approach, combining theoretical analysis and simulation studies of current relays in the face of cyber-attacks. Various cyber-attack scenarios, including malicious communication interference, data manipulation, and false data injection attacks, are considered to gauge the relay's ability to operate accurately and swiftly under adversarial conditions. This research has simulated various attacks in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment for a two-bus system model. Simulations are performed to replicate potential cyber threats and measure the impact on protection relay operations. The study of this research provides insightful information into the vulnerabilities of current-based relays to cyber intrusions and offers practical recommendations for enhancing their cybersecurity posture.

articleTitle: Discriminating Emotional Insights Using HHS Features of EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Emotion recognition using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals has recently garnered significant attention from researchers owing to its broad applications in clinical settings, affective computing, and other related domains. Effectively capturing emotional insights and improving recognition accuracy has been a critical challenge in traditional EEG-based emotion detection methods. This study introduces a novel algorithm for automatic emotion recognition by computing Hilbert Huang Spectrum (HHS) features of EEG and input to a Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM). The proposed framework captures time-frequency domain attributes from various rhythms of the EEG signal obtained using DWT to form a feature matrix. A fine-tuned Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) processed HHS features and classified emotions into distinct classes. The proposed approach performance is assessed using three well-known open-source databases, DEAP, SEED, and SEED-IV, reporting classification accuracy of 95.8%, 97.2%, and 98.6% for 10-fold cross-validation experiments. The suggested method exhibited superior emotion recognition performance compared to most of the existing machine learning-based approaches.

articleTitle: Advancing Data Sovereignty in Distributed Environments: An In-Depth Exploration of Data Localization Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Data localization in distributed computing has gotten a lot of attention because it has the potential to improve data sovereignty, make sure regulations are followed, and make data easier to access. However, this practice also brings forth a multitude of challenges and threats to cybersecurity, data privacy, and overall information security. In this comprehensive survey paper, we delve into the complex landscape of challenges and threats associated with data localization in distributed computing environments. We explore the intricate interplay between data localization, distributed infrastructure, cybersecurity, and privacy concerns. This paper provides an in-depth analysis of various challenges such as regulatory compliance, data integrity, authentication, and access control, along with potential threats like data breaches, insider attacks, and unauthorized access. Furthermore, we investigate the state-of-the-art security mechanisms, encryption techniques, privacy-preserving methods, and access control strategies that researchers and practitioners have developed to address these challenges. Through this survey, we aim to provide a comprehensive overview of the critical issues surrounding data localization within cloud computing and shed light on the emerging trends and potential solutions that can pave the way for secure and privacy-aware data localization practices.

articleTitle: Demand Side Management and Voltage Control through Smart Inverter Enabled DER with Networked Micro-Grid System
